chapters.title: Shared Ideals
chapters.mission: Complete 3 battles using Sleep Star: Impact Wolf
chapters.summary: Usopp bonds with a hero over their shared belief in protecting the innocent. They discuss their motivations and learn from each other's experiences.
chapters.bondRewardHint: Sleep duration increases.

friendshipCampaign.overview: Usopp, despite his cowardly tendencies, dreams of being a brave warrior of the sea. This campaign explores his journey to overcome his fears, honing his tactical skills and finding strength in his friendships with unlikely allies, ultimately realizing that true bravery isn't the absence of fear, but acting in spite of it.

friendshipCampaign.dailyNode: Every day, Usopp sets up a 'Trap Course' where players must navigate a series of increasingly difficult obstacles created by Usopp's Rubber Band of Doom and Lying Bait, earning friendship points and resource materials for each successful run. Completing it provides a funny dialogue exchange where Usopp brags (or complains) about the player's performance.

character_v1.playstyle: Defensive Support with Counter-Attack Potential
character_v1.teamSynergy: Kristoff synergizes well with durable allies who can benefit from increased defense and luck. He also works effectively with teams that focus on controlling the battlefield, allowing him to set up devastating counter-attacks with 'Avalanche Counter'. Allies who can reliably trigger enemy Ultimates greatly enhance his effectiveness.
character_v1.tierSummary: Kristoff's kit suffers from disjointed scaling and role conflict; 'Sven's Sniff Out' provides crucial team-wide evasion but its synergy with his tank-leaning abilities is weak. 'Reindeer Games' is a poorly-defined stacking mechanic that offers negligible benefits, overshadowed by superior support options like Sakura Haruno who offer more direct and impactful buffs. 'Avalanche Counter', while visually impressive, lacks the burst disruption to effectively interrupt critical enemy ultimates compared to dedicated controllers. His 'Frozen Fortification' passive is reliant on external factors to even function, resulting in inconsistent and ultimately negligible damage output, placing him firmly in mid-tier A due to niche defensive utility but overall lack of cohesive synergy.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Kristoff's kit revolves around the 'Reindeer Games' mechanic, enhancing both his defensive capabilities and counter-attack potential. 'Frozen Fortification' rewards defensive play, while 'Avalanche Counter' punishes aggressive enemy strategies. The abilities work in harmony to protect allies and disrupt enemies.

All allies and enemies within the radius gain 'Aura Resonance' for 5 seconds. Allies with Aura Resonance gain 20% lifesteal. Enemies with Aura Resonance have their healing reduced by 30%. abilities.flavorQuote: Feel the full power of my Aura!

character_v1.playstyle: Aura Weaver - Strategic Buff/Debuff Support
character_v1.teamSynergy: Riolu synergizes well with aggressive melee carries and mages who benefit from increased movement speed, lifesteal, and reduced enemy magic resistance. He provides crucial support, peeling, and team fight initiation capabilities. His ability to manipulate enemy healing and attack damage also makes him an effective counter against sustain-heavy compositions.
character_v1.tierSummary: Riolu's S-tier designation is questionable; Aura Sense provides map awareness, but his kit struggles to synergize as a dedicated tank compared to peers. Force Palm offers limited, single-target CC, while Quick Guard's short duration and aura cost make it an inefficient shield. Vacuum Wave's AoE is inconsistent, and Emanation Burst, while offering invulnerability, consumes all Aura, leaving Riolu vulnerable post-cast. His reliance on Aura management and telegraphed invulnerability frames hinder his tanking capabilities against true S-tier anchors like Minnie Mouse or E.T..
character_v1.internalSynergy: Riolu's kit revolves around building and spending Aura strategically. 'Aura Sense' fuels his abilities, while 'Force Palm', 'Quick Guard', and 'Vacuum Wave' provide impactful effects amplified by Aura consumption and 'Aura Resonance'. 'Emanation Burst' is a high-impact ultimate that can turn the tide of team fights through invulnerability, damage, healing, and extended Aura Resonance effects.

character_v1.playstyle: Burst Support
character_v1.teamSynergy: Mei excels in aggressive team compositions that benefit from burst healing, damage reduction, and crowd control. Her I-frames and invulnerability provided by 'Pandapocalypse 2002' can be used to initiate fights or protect allies from powerful ultimates, while her debuffs and buffs enhance the team's overall damage output and survivability.
character_v1.tierSummary: Meilin Lee's kit exhibits strong tank synergy via HP scaling and inherent tenacity, though Emotional Overflow management is paramount. Compared to S-tier peers like E.T., her area control is less reliable, relying on 'Growing Pains' burst. Viability hinges on 'Inner Turmoil' and 'Pandapocalypse 2002' transformations for I-frames/healing but lacks the raw disruption of top-tier tanks. 'Stuffed Animal Shield' needs strategic deployment to avoid over-extension, and 'Panda Hug' is a risky heal if poorly positioned; overall, skilled play minimizes these flaws.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Mei's kit revolves around rapidly filling her 'Emotional Overflow' to transform into her Red Panda form, which significantly enhances her support and tanking capabilities. She provides shields, heals, and crowd control, all amplified during her transformation. Her passive allows her to build overflow from taking damage, blocking and dodging, encouraging her to stay in the fight.

upgrades: (Enhancement) Increase 'Foresight' duration by 1 second.

abilities.description: Yoda transcends the physical realm, momentarily becoming one with the Force, a beacon of light and power for his allies. For a fleeting 1.5 seconds, Yoda enters a state of pure invulnerability, untouchable by any harm as he channels the cosmic energy. Upon achieving this momentary enlightenment, Yoda projects a vast, shimmering field of Force energy, extending outwards in a massive circle. Enemies caught within this circle of influence immediately feel their connection to the Force disrupted, becoming 'Stunted' for 3 seconds, silencing their abilities and dampening their offensive capabilities by reducing damage output by 15%. Simultaneously, allies bathed in the Force's glow experience a surge of empowerment, gaining 'Foresight' for 7 seconds, increasing their critical hit chance by 35% and movement speed by 20%. This profound connection to the Force requires time to replenish, resulting in a cooldown of 90 seconds before Yoda can guide his allies again.

character_v1.playstyle: Tactical Debuffer & Support
character_v1.teamSynergy: Yoda synergizes well with damage-dealing characters who can benefit from the attack speed and damage boosts provided by Insight and Empowered. His crowd control abilities also help protect squishy carries and allow them to deal damage more safely. Champions that benefit greatly from ability haste, such as mages or support characters with impactful cooldowns, also benefit significantly from Yoda's presence.
character_v1.tierSummary: Yoda's S-tier assassin status is bolstered by potent disruption and scaling damage, synergizing 'Mind Trick' with 'Masterful Guidance' for exponential stat growth. Compared to peers like Tao, his reliance on setup and sustained engagements differentiates him, demanding precise ability sequencing. 'Force Absorb' provides crucial survivability, enabling aggressive plays, while 'Unleash the Force' solidifies team fight dominance via widespread debuffs. However, vulnerability to burst damage and reliance on 'Clarity' stacks limit his overall effectiveness, requiring careful positioning and target selection to optimize assassination potential, making his tier placement questionable given the crowded assassin role at S-tier.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Yoda's kit revolves around generating Clarity stacks through disrupting enemies and providing support, then using the stacks to empower his team with Insight, enhancing their attack speed and ability usage. Force Push and Mind Trick provide crowd control, while Force Absorb allows Yoda to survive long enough to build up Clarity stacks. Unleash the Force is the ultimate expression of this synergy, combining crowd control with a significant damage boost for allies.

abilities.description: Zoro's relentless three-sword style seeks to leave lasting scars on any opponent daring to face him. Each of Zoro's basic attacks carries a 15% chance to inflict 'Pierced,' a grievous wound that ignores all defenses and deals true damage to the target. This damage equates to 2% of the target's maximum health, dealt over a 3-second duration, showcasing the depth of Zoro's strikes. When Zoro channels his Haki, his resolve intensifies. With each stack of 'Haki Imbued,' the probability of inflicting 'Pierced' escalates by 2%, reaching a maximum of 25% at five stacks, ensuring that enemies constantly feel the bite of his swords. Furthermore, Zoro's iron will grants him 10% tenacity, shortening the duration of crowd control effects such as stuns or slows, allowing him to stay in the fray and continue his relentless assault. Zoro's mastery extends his reach, granting an additional 50 units of attack range, allowing him to strike from a safer distance while maintaining control of the battlefield. The effects of each 'Pierced' application are independent, their 3-second timers unaffected by subsequent attacks, ensuring that the wounds accumulate and the pressure mounts. This passive transforms Zoro into an assassin who punishes enemy mistakes, with unavoidable damage wearing down even the sturdiest foes.

character_v1.playstyle: Aggressive, Resource Management
character_v1.teamSynergy: Zoro benefits from allies who can provide crowd control or engage in team fights, allowing him to safely build and expend Haki Imbued stacks. He can also act as a secondary damage threat, punishing enemies who focus on other targets.
character_v1.tierSummary: Zoro's viability stems from 'Unwavering Resolve' scaling linearly with sustained combat and the burst potential of 'Ashura', but his reliance on basic attacks and predictable counter (Lion's Song) leaves him vulnerable to disruption. Compared to top-tier damage dealers, Zoro lacks inherent mobility and/or innate defense, rendering him overly reliant on favorable matchups. 'Blade Mastery' provides a marginal true damage buff, which is insufficient to compensate for his shortcomings against armored opponents. Though his damage output is respectable in extended fights, Zoro's lack of a reliable engage or escape tool relegates him to a high-risk, high-reward niche.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Zoro's kit revolves around maintaining Haki Imbued stacks to empower his abilities. Lion's Song provides a defensive option and a way to gain stacks, while Oni Giri is a reliable damage dealer and stack consumer. Ashura serves as a powerful offensive ultimate, amplifying Zoro's damage and stack generation.

abilities.description: Mitotic Regeneration epitomizes Sakura's unparalleled control over cellular mitosis, manifesting as a potent healing wave. Upon activation, Sakura channels chakra into accelerated cellular division, unleashing a surging tide of restorative energy. This wave emanates outwards in a cone-shaped area, primarily targeting allies, but also possesses a unique interaction with enemies. For allies, the wave instantly restores a significant portion of their health, scaling dynamically with Sakura's maximum HP and Healing Power stats. Furthermore, it applies a Regen buff, granting sustained healing over time, with the duration and potency also scaling with Sakura's stats. Crucially, the wave's interaction with enemies inflicts a temporary 'Cellular Instability' debuff; rather than directly damaging foes, it disrupts their natural healing processes, effectively reducing their healing received from all sources for a short duration. This disruption is particularly effective against enemies that rely on self-healing or regeneration, making it a valuable tactical tool. Moreover, 'Cellular Instability' has a chance to trigger a secondary effect, causing a minor burst of damage-over-time effect proportional to the initial healing reduction. This ability is core to Sakura's role as a supportive healer, enabling her to sustain her team while simultaneously hindering enemy sustain strategies.

It is a pivotal ability that requires strategic timing and positioning to maximize its effectiveness.
abilities.flavorQuote: This is the power of the Strength of a Hundred Seal!

character_v1.playstyle: Burst Healer, Disruption Specialist
character_v1.teamSynergy: Sakura excels in teams that benefit from sustained healing and disruption. She synergizes well with damage dealers who can capitalize on her stuns and debuffs, as well as tanks who can protect her while she builds Chakra Focus.
character_v1.tierSummary: Sakura's S-tier placement is questionable; while her healing output is significant, it's gated behind Chakra Focus, creating a vulnerability window. 'Strength of a Hundred: Concussion' offers burst stun, but its unreliable targeting undermines its value. Compared to peers like Tao and Blossom, her supportive capabilities lack the immediate impact and control necessary for top-tier play. Effective viability hinges solely on 'Creation Rebirth: Miracle Heal' to swing team fights, rendering her kit otherwise disjointed and predictable. Lacks synergistic ability combinations compared to tier peers, such as the consistent lockdown offered by Android 18.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Sakura's kit revolves around building Chakra Focus and strategically using her abilities to heal, disrupt, and empower her team. Her passive encourages active participation in combat and skillful healing to maximize her effectiveness.

character_v1.playstyle: Aggressive Brawler
character_v1.teamSynergy: Luffy excels in teams that can provide sustain and crowd control, allowing him to safely build Haki and unleash his powerful Gear transformations. He benefits from allies who can amplify his damage output or provide shields to protect him while he is vulnerable after his transformations end.
character_v1.tierSummary: Luffy's A tier placement is generous; while Gear transformations offer burst potential, their short durations and vulnerability to debuff-heavy teams cripple sustained damage output. Haki Infusion provides marginal utility compared to dedicated buffing peers, and his reliance on single-target damage in a meta saturated with AoE controllers like Eleven renders him inconsistent. The delayed payoff from Haki stacking conflicts with the aggressive nature of Gear 2nd, forcing suboptimal play patterns. Compared to equally-ranked tanks like Meilin Lee or Thragg, Luffy provides neither the immediate disruption nor sustained survivability to justify his Melee Carry classification; ultimately, he's a feast-or-famine character dependent on matchup lottery.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Luffy's abilities synergize around building Haki, transforming into different Gears, and utilizing those forms to deal damage. Each Gear form drastically changes his playstyle, making him versatile in different combat situations.

abilities.description: Gertie, fueled by boundless imagination and the sheer force of her childhood whimsy, momentarily opens a gateway to the realm of make-believe, unleashing a chaotic swarm of her uniquely terrifying imaginary friends upon her chosen target. Selecting a single enemy champion within a generous range of 650 units, Gertie conjures a phantasmagorical horde of playful yet perilous entities that assail the target with unrestrained fervor for 2.5 seconds. Each imaginary friend relentlessly claws and bites, inflicting a base 25 (+15% of Gertie's AP) magic damage per strike, with an additional 5 (+2% of Gertie's AP) applied per strike for each active stack of 'Hide and Seek' on Gertie. Further amplifying the onslaught, Gertie's focus affects the frequency of these phantom attacks: for every 10% of Gertie's current Focus bar, the number of attacks increase by 5%, up to a maximum of 50% extra attacks. These spectral assailants not only inflict damage, but also sow confusion and disorientation, applying a 20% slow to the enemy's movement speed for the duration of the barrage. character_v1.playstyle: Healer/Buffer focused on plant-based effects and team synergy.

character_v1.tierSummary: Gertie's A-tier support ranking hinges on her potent Empathic Bloom passive, enabling reactive AoE healing and utility. Protective Embrace is a crucial defensive tool, though its short duration demands precise timing; E.T.'s Blessing, while impactful, is telegraphed and susceptible to disruption, ultimately positioning Gertie as a situational support reliant on team coordination to maximize her reactive kit.

Gentle Nurture and Protective Embrace consume Bloom for increased effects.

This ally's critical hit chance is increased by 12% and their evasion rate is improved by 8%, making them more likely to land devastating blows and dodge incoming attacks, reflecting Mickey's knack for elevating those around him to perform at their best, especially in moments of high-pressure combat. In addition, the closest ally will receive 5% increased movement speed, allowing them to more effectively move and weave through team fights or kite enemies.

abilities.description: Mickey's inherent optimism shines brightest when his friends are in danger. Whenever an allied hero's health plummets below 30%, Mickey's 'Cheerful Tune' ability immediately has its cooldown reset, allowing him to swiftly come to their aid. The next cast of 'Cheerful Tune' on that ally is supercharged, amplified with additional healing power. The restored health jumps by 10% of the ally's missing health plus an amount that scales with 40% of Mickey's magic attack, ensuring a substantial boost in their time of need. To prevent abuse and maintain balance, this effect can trigger only once every 15 seconds per individual ally. Mickey's unwavering belief in his friends, represented by this passive, ensures they have a much better shot at surviving critical situations, bolstering their resolve to continue the fight. During these moments, he stands tall.

abilities.description: Mickey Mouse begins whistling a lively tune, drastically increasing the attack speed and movement speed of all allies for 8 seconds. During this time, allies also gain a temporary shield that absorbs a moderate amount of damage, protecting them from incoming attacks. The shield's strength scales with Mickey's magic defense. This ultimate ability symbolizes Mickey's can-do attitude and ability to inspire his team, creating a powerful surge of energy and resilience that can turn the tide of battle. It embodies Mickey's leadership role and his infectious enthusiasm.
abilities.flavorQuote: Let's get to it, everyone!

character_v1.playstyle: Supportive Buffer
character_v1.teamSynergy: Mickey pairs well with damage-focused characters who benefit from increased speed and attack. His healing and shielding capabilities make him a reliable support for front-line fighters, while his speed buffs can significantly enhance the mobility of agile characters. He generally enables carries, tank, and other damage dealers to stay alive and fight longer.
character_v1.tierSummary: Mickey Mouse's kit suffers from severe scaling issues and lacks impactful healing output, rendering him wholly unviable as a primary healer in the current meta; his reliance on low-value stat buffs and conditional triggers (Optimistic Outlook) provides insufficient utility compared to higher-tier support options. Goodwill Gestures' negligible stat bonuses and Whistle While You Work's unfocused buff spread fail to deliver meaningful team fight advantages, especially compared to peers like dedicated buffers or burst healers; further exacerbating Mickey's problems is his competition with burst oriented healing heros like Gojo Satoru and Megumi Fushiguro, who at least offer more impactful conditional cc. Mickey’s only strength is his evasion increase on White Glove Treatment, but that pales in comparison to the damage and sustain offered by meta healers.

tips: Prioritize allies who are taking damage with 'Cheerful Tune' to maximize its shield effect.
Use 'White Glove Treatment' to quickly reposition allies or save them from danger with speed and evasion.
Save 'Whistle While You Work' for crucial moments when your team needs a burst of speed and protection, like during a focused enemy attack.
strategyData.overview: Mickey Mouse is a dedicated healer who focuses on keeping his team alive through burst heals, shields, and speed boosts. He's very reliant on staying near his allies, and benefits from allies who can use the extra speed he provides.
strategyData.counterplay: Focus fire Mickey Mouse down before he can react, as he doesn't have any self-preserving abilities. CC him and watch his allies crumble.

Richard's Trivia buff and the Speed from Trunks help push this momentum.

His 'Goodwill Gestures' passive complements his active abilities, creating a consistent support presence. His ultimate ability amplifies the effects of his other skills, making him a valuable asset in team fights.

abilities.description: Minnie Mouse focuses her cheerful spirit, weaving a vibrant ribbon of pure, restorative energy directly towards the targeted ally. This ribbon, shimmering with positive vibes, instantly grants a burst of healing equal to Minnie's base HP plus a scaling factor based on her own maximum HP. This ensures that the Ribbon Remedy remains effective, patching up even the burliest of teammates. As the ribbon makes contact, it also emanates a soothing aura. This aura provides a secondary heal to the targeted ally, mending them for 25% of the initial heal over the course of 3 seconds; thus the healing is delivered in 3 ticks of even magnitude, each occurring precisely 1 second apart. Furthermore, any teammate within a short radius of the primary target is also revitalized, receiving an immediate heal equal to 10% of Minnie's total HP, reinforcing Minnie's role as the team's unwavering bastion of healing and support, turning the tide of battle with every well-placed Ribbon Remedy.

abilities.description: From her seemingly endless collection of bows, Minnie magically conjures a life-sized Polka-Dot Bow, spending 50 Bow Fabric in the process. As the bow makes contact, a wave of invigorating polka-dots washes over the target, instantly restoring X hit points (scaling with Minnie's magic attack power). More than just a simple heal, the polka-dots weave a protective 'Bow-tique Barrier' around the ally, boosting their armor and magic resistance by 15% and granting them 10 tenacity, making them more resistant to disabling effects, for a duration of 4 seconds. Should the targeted ally already be at peak health, the Polka-Dot Panacea transforms into a temporary shield, absorbing damage equal to 20% of the initial healing amount. This protective barrier lasts for 3 seconds, providing crucial buffer against incoming attacks. Minnie can use Polka-Dot Panacea again after a cooldown of 8 seconds, ensuring a steady flow of healing and supportive buffs to keep her teammates in tip-top shape throughout the fray.

abilities.description: Minnie's inherent charm and boundless creativity allow her to passively accumulate Polka Dot Energy, a resource vital to her most dazzling creations and empowering performances. She gains 5 Polka Dot Energy every second, automatically stockpiling this magical essence up to a maximum of 200. After Minnie unleashes an active ability fueled by Polka Dot Energy, her next basic attack within a 5-second window becomes imbued with shimmering polka dot magic, dealing bonus magic damage equal to a delightful 10% of the Polka Dot Energy expended. For example, if Minnie casts an ability costing 100 Polka Dot Energy, her subsequent basic attack will inflict an additional 10 magic damage. Should Minnie's Polka Dot Energy reserves reach their peak of 200, she experiences a burst of pure joy, resulting in a 10% increase to her movement speed. This enhanced mobility persists until she spends any amount of Polka Dot Energy, reminding everyone that even the smallest bow packs a significant punch! Strategic use of her abilities and careful management of her Polka Dot Energy are critical for Minnie to maximize her effectiveness on the battlefield, allowing her to weave a tapestry of charm and combat prowess that leaves enemies bewildered and allies inspired.

Enemies with 'Sweet Notes' take X (scales with magic atk) magic damage per second. Sweet Notes last for 3 seconds and can stack up to 3 times, increasing the healing or damage by 50% per stack. abilities.name: Bow-hemian Rhapsody
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Nerf: reduced peak potency ~13% and slightly longer ramp-up.
abilities.description: Minnie unleashes her ultimate creation, crafting a 'Rainbow Bow' at the cost of all remaining Bow Fabric. She then fires the bow into the sky, creating a dazzling spectacle. Allies within a large radius gain increased attack damage and magic damage, scaling with the amount of Bow Fabric consumed (1% per 5 Bow Fabric), for 8 seconds. Enemies within the same radius are stunned for 1 second and then take damage over time, also scaling with the amount of Bow Fabric consumed (X magic damage per second for 5 seconds, scaling with magic atk, 0.5% per 5 Bow Fabric). After casting, Minnie is invigorated, gaining 20% cooldown reduction for 6 seconds. Consuming all Bow Fabric ensures maximum impact, but timing is crucial.
abilities.flavorQuote: A symphony of support, a crescendo of charm!

character_v1.playstyle: Versatile buff and heal-oriented support, excels in enhancing allies and providing sustained healing while weaving in light damage and utility.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Minnie excels in teams that benefit from sustained healing and damage amplification. Her buffs to attack and magic damage, combined with her defensive support, make her an ideal partner for damage-heavy compositions. She synergizes well with allies who can capitalize on the increased damage output and benefit from the defensive buffs provided by her abilities.
character_v1.tierSummary: Minnie's SS tier placement is questionable; while *Bow-hemian Rhapsody* provides decent AoE control and damage, its complete Fabric reliance creates severe vulnerability. Compared to actual top-tier supports like E.T. or offensive threats like Tao, she lacks immediate impact and consistent pressure. Her role synergy suffers from subpar scaling on *Ribbon Remedy* and unreliable damage from *Polka-Dot Pop*, especially in a roster oversaturated with DoT. *Sweetheart Serenade's* stacking heal is her only redeeming factor, yet it's easily countered by burst damage, making her a situational, win-more pick that struggles in neutral and falls apart under pressure, further burdened by her archetype's support population.

tips: Optimize Bow Fabric: The name of the game is Bow Fabric! Track the rate you're generating it, and remember you're wasting potential by sitting at max Fabric.
Prioritize Targets: Ribbon Remedy's shield can bait enemies into focusing the shielded target. Polka-Dot Pop is crucial for peeling; hitting debuffed enemies extends its duration.
Time Sweetheart Serenade: Use this when your team can capitalize on the healing or damage. It's a powerful tool in extended fights, but a waste if used carelessly.
strategyData.overview: Minnie Mouse is a resource-dependent Glamour Support who wants to weave in and out of fights. You'll spend most of your time passively gathering Bow Fabric, then strategically spending it to buff allies or debuff enemies. If you don't focus on resource management, you will not be effective with this character.
strategyData.counterplay: Shut down Minnie's Bow Fabric generation or punish her for overspending it. Burst her down when she has low Fabric, since her ability to buff and debuff is directly tied to it. CCing her during ultimate severely reduces the radius that allies and enemies are buffed/debuffed.

teamLineups.note: This comp focuses on amplifying Minnie's Defense buffing capabilities by including tanks and bruisers that benefit from increased defense and tenacity. Frog and Tatsuki get stronger with high Def values, and are further enhanced by Minnie's healing.

character_v1.internalSynergy: Minnie's kit revolves around her 'Bow-tique' mechanic, with her abilities synergizing to maximize Bow Fabric generation and consumption. 'Bow-tique Brilliance' fuels her other abilities, while 'Ribbon Remedy' and 'Polka-Dot Pop' provide a mix of healing, buffing, debuffing, and damage. 'Sweetheart Serenade' amplifies her sustained healing or damage output, and 'Bow-hemian Rhapsody' provides a game-changing ultimate that scales with her Bow Fabric management.

abilities.description: Donald steels his nerves, drawing upon the salty wisdom of a thousand voyages, manifesting a shimmering bubble of pure, unfettered annoyance! For 4 seconds, Donald gains a shield that absorbs incoming damage, protecting him from harm. The shield's strength scales with Donald's level, providing significant damage mitigation, allowing him to weather even the stormiest of encounters. While this irascible barrier is active, Donald's speed increases by 20%, allowing him to navigate the battlefield with surprising agility, deftly dodging attacks and positioning himself for maximum disruptive impact. However, the intensity of his focus causes a slight dip in his usual offensive capabilities, reducing his attack damage by 15%. The shield also grants Donald immunity to crowd control effects, ensuring that he can't be stunned, silenced, or otherwise hindered during this crucial period. Even if the shield is shattered prematurely by an overwhelming onslaught, the immunity to crowd control remains for the full 4 second duration, a testament to Donald's sheer stubbornness. Once the shield dissipates, whether broken or expired, the concentrated frustration builds to a boiling point, imbuing his next auto-attack with bonus damage equal to 50% of the damage the shield absorbed, punishing his foes for daring to challenge his seaworthy spirit. Finally, as the last vestiges of the shield fade, Donald gains 10% evasion for 2 seconds, allowing him to deftly avoid incoming attacks and maintain his position in the fray, a testament to his surprisingly nimble footwork. Activating this ability also generates 15 Rage, fueling his other abilities.

character_v1.playstyle: Aggressive Marksman
character_v1.teamSynergy: Donald benefits from allies who can provide crowd control to help him land his inaccurate attacks, or those who can mitigate damage to keep him alive while he's in his vulnerable 'Furious' state. Support characters that can grant him temporary invincibility or speed boosts can maximize his damage output during these periods.
character_v1.tierSummary: Donald's A-tier bruiser placement is justified by strong rage-fueled offensive output, but he suffers from inconsistent AoE targeting and reliance on Volatile Temper for scaling. He struggles against true tanks due to lacking penetration, unlike other top-tier bruisers; Sailor's Fury offers brief CC immunity but is often insufficient against dedicated controllers. Phooey Barrage and Ultimate Outburst are his defining tools, offering burst potential, though their unreliability hurts his consistency compared to more focused damage dealers. Donald's kit synergizes adequately for sustained damage, but he falls short of S-tier due to a lack of specialized strengths compared to role contemporaries.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Donald's abilities are designed to intentionally build up his 'Rage' quickly, allowing him to reach his 'Furious' state frequently. However, managing the negative effects of high Rage and the 'Exhausted' debuff is crucial for sustained effectiveness.

character_v1.tierSummary: Frog's kit suffers from mediocre scaling and a lack of hard CC beyond his ultimate, hindering his tanking potential compared to superior frontline options. Amphibian Armor incentivizes close-quarters ally stacking, but offers insufficient protection to justify the inherent risk. Water Slash's slow is unreliable, and Slurp Heal provides inadequate burst healing to rescue allies in critical situations, diminishing his support capabilities. Leap of Faith's shield is easily burst through, and Frog Squash's delayed activation makes it telegraphed and avoidable, further cementing his position as a situational A-tier tank overshadowed by more consistent performers like Thragg and Skulker, who offer better damage mitigation and disruption.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Frog's kit revolves around protecting allies. Amphibian Armor encourages him to stay close, Slurp Heal keeps them alive, Leap of Faith allows for quick repositioning to protect them, and Frog Squash provides a burst of healing in a teamfight. When Michael has max stacks, his next basic attack will stun the target for 0.75 seconds.
abilities.flavorQuote: Not on my watch!

abilities.name: Communicator Setup
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Nerf: reduced peak potency ~11% and slightly longer ramp-up.
abilities.description: Michael deploys a makeshift 'Communicator' at a targeted location. The Communicator passively grants nearby allies a buff based on their role, stacking up to 3 times. Damage roles gain a 5% attack damage increase per stack, Tank roles gain a 3% damage reduction per stack, and Support roles gain a 5% increase to healing and shielding effectiveness per stack. The Communicator has a limited health pool and can be destroyed by enemies. It lasts for 15 seconds. Cooldown of 20 seconds. Consumes 60 energy.
abilities.flavorQuote: Let's see if we can boost the signal!

abilities.name: Beacon of Hope
upgrades: (Bugfix) Resolved inconsistent trigger interactions reported in live matches (occurrence ~46%).
abilities.description: Michael channels his inner strength, creating a powerful beacon using the Communicator. All allies within a large radius gain increased attack speed and lifesteal for 8 seconds. Attack speed is increased by 20% and lifesteal is increased by 15%. Additionally, the Communicator emits a pulse of energy every 2 seconds, healing allies for X health, scaling with Michael's max HP. This ability requires a fully charged ultimate bar and consumes the active Communicator if one is present, enhancing the heal by 50%.
abilities.flavorQuote: We're not giving up now!

character_v1.playstyle: Protective Buffer
character_v1.teamSynergy: Michael excels in teams that benefit from sustained buffs and protection. He is particularly effective with damage dealers who rely on attack speed and lifesteal, and tanks who benefit from damage reduction. His ability to strategically deploy the Communicator and provide emergency heals makes him a valuable asset in team fights.
character_v1.tierSummary: Michael's A-tier support ranking is propped up by Communicator Setup's stacked buffs and Beacon of Hope's potent AoE heal/lifesteal; however, his kit lacks hard CC, limiting synergy in a meta where controllers heavily influence pacing. While Makeshift Shield offers burst protection, it's less reliable than consistent mitigation from peers like Arceus. Protective Instincts is reactive, and its inconsistent trigger condition makes it unreliable compared to proactive healing. Thus, Michael's viability hinges on aggressive team compositions that capitalize on raw stat buffs rather than strategic control, leaving him vulnerable in more diverse matchups.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Michael's kit revolves around protecting and buffing his allies. Makeshift Shield offers immediate protection, while Emergency Rations provides sustain. Protective Instincts rewards him for mitigating damage to allies, and Communicator Setup provides a strategic advantage. Beacon of Hope serves as a strong team-wide buff and heal, synergizing with his other supportive abilities.

character_v1.name: Thragg

Lv100: base damage increases and minor utility interaction
mechanics: Ranged single strike.

abilities.name: Viltrumite Might (Passive)
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
(Bugfix) Resolved inconsistent trigger interactions reported in live matches (occurrence ~49%).
(Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
abilities.description: Thragg embodies the pinnacle of Viltrumite resilience. For every 5% of his maximum health he loses, he gains 2% bonus attack damage and 3% tenacity, stacking up to a maximum of 40% bonus attack damage and 60% tenacity. This effect persists until Thragg is fully healed. Additionally, when Thragg reaches 50% health, he gains a permanent 10% damage reduction. The bonus attack damage affects both basic attacks and abilities, amplifying his offensive capabilities as he takes damage. The tenacity reduces the duration of crowd control effects, making him increasingly difficult to lock down.
abilities.flavorQuote: Pain is but a pathway to greater power.

abilities.name: Regent's Fury
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
abilities.description: Thragg unleashes a series of rapid punches in a cone in front of him, dealing X physical damage to all enemies hit over 2 seconds. Enemies hit by Regent's Fury are also slowed by 20% for 1 second. If Thragg has taken more than 30% of his maximum health in damage, the slow is increased to 40% and also applies a stacking debuff that reduces enemy armor by 5% for 3 seconds, stacking up to 3 times. This ability benefits greatly from 'Viltrumite Might,' as bonus damage from the passive directly increases the damage output of the rapid punches.
abilities.flavorQuote: Feel the might of a Regent's wrath!

abilities.name: Viltrumite Charge
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
(Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
abilities.description: Thragg charges forward a short distance, becoming immune to crowd control effects during the charge. If he collides with an enemy, he deals X physical damage and knocks them up into the air for 0.75 seconds. If Thragg's 'Viltrumite Might' passive is active, the knock-up duration is increased to 1.25 seconds. Furthermore, the first enemy hit is marked for 5 seconds. Thragg's next basic attack against a marked target deals bonus true damage equal to 8% of Thragg's maximum health, reinforcing his role as a powerful, sustained damage dealer.
abilities.flavorQuote: The Empire's will is an unstoppable force!

abilities.name: Unbreakable Resolve
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
abilities.description: Thragg hardens his body, gaining a shield equal to 15% of his maximum health for 4 seconds. While the shield is active, Thragg's attack damage is increased by 10%. If the shield is broken before the duration ends, Thragg releases a shockwave, dealing X magic damage to nearby enemies and healing himself for 10% of the damage dealt. Additionally, if Thragg has taken more than 50% of his maximum health in damage, the shield strength is increased to 25% of his maximum health, making him even more durable in critical situations.
abilities.flavorQuote: My resolve is absolute!

abilities.name: Wrath of the Regent (Ultimate)
abilities.description: Thragg unleashes his full power, becoming enraged for 10 seconds. While enraged, Thragg gains 30% bonus attack damage, 20% movement speed, and his 'Viltrumite Might' passive effects are doubled. During this time, Thragg's basic attacks cleave, dealing 50% of the damage to enemies near his target. At the end of the duration, Thragg releases a devastating roar, dealing X true damage to all enemies within a large radius and stunning them for 1.5 seconds. This ability encapsulates Thragg's role as a powerhouse that thrives in extended combat, dealing increased sustained damage.
abilities.flavorQuote: You will witness true Viltrumite power!

character_v1.playstyle: Aggressive, Sustained Combat, Punisher
character_v1.teamSynergy: Thragg synergizes well with teams that can provide healing and sustain, allowing him to maximize the effects of 'Viltrumite Might.' He also benefits from allies who can apply crowd control, setting up opportunities for his high-damage abilities. Characters that can amplify his damage or provide additional protection further enhance his effectiveness in team fights.
character_v1.tierSummary: Thragg's kit suffers from redundancy, particularly with other SS-tier tanks; his reliance on HP-based scaling via 'Viltrumite Might' is statistically inferior to E.T.'s %-damage reduction. 'Regent's Fury' offers negligible healing and its slow is easily countered, while 'Viltrumite Charge' provides limited utility due to its short range and the roster's prevalence of hyper-armor. 'Unbreakable Resolve's' shield is insufficient to protect against burst damage common at this tier, making it statistically ineffective compared to Tao or Blossom's crowd control. 'Wrath of the Regent', despite its ultimate status, is outclassed by Omniman's superior damage output and crowd control, solidifying Thragg as an underperforming SS-tier tank with scaling problems and a kit that lacks the synergy to compete.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Thragg's kit is designed around sustained combat, with his passive 'Viltrumite Might' providing scaling damage and tenacity as he takes damage. His abilities 'Regent's Fury,' 'Viltrumite Charge,' and 'Unbreakable Resolve' all benefit from this passive, creating a powerful feedback loop that rewards aggressive play and punishes enemies for focusing him. 'Wrath of the Regent' amplifies all these effects, making him an unstoppable force during its duration.

character_v1.name: Arceus

abilities.name: Basic Attack

abilities.name: Elemental Shift
abilities.description: Arceus constantly cycles through elemental Plates in a set order: Fire, Water, Grass, Electric. Each Plate grants different effects. When on Fire Plate, allies within a medium radius gain 10% increased attack damage. While on Water Plate, allies gain 10% increased magic defense. While on Grass Plate, allies within a medium radius are healed for 2% of their maximum HP every second. While on Electric Plate, enemies within a medium radius have their movement speed reduced by 15%. These effects last as long as Arceus maintains the corresponding Plate and linger for 1 second after switching. The cycle continues indefinitely, providing a dynamic ebb and flow of elemental buffs and debuffs.
abilities.flavorQuote: The essence of creation flows through me, adapting to the needs of all.

abilities.name: Judgment Bolt
abilities.description: Arceus unleashes a Judgment Bolt, the type of which corresponds to the current active Elemental Plate. Fire Judgment deals damage in a line and inflicts a burn, dealing 5% of the target's maximum HP as damage over 3 seconds. Water Judgment creates a small area of effect that slows enemies by 25% for 2 seconds. Grass Judgment heals allies in a small area for 10% of their maximum HP. Electric Judgment stuns the primary target for 0.75 seconds. The bolt travels a medium distance and has a moderate cooldown of 8 seconds. The specific effect is determined at the moment of casting based on the current active Elemental Plate.
abilities.flavorQuote: By my judgment, the elements shall bend to my will!

abilities.name: Cosmic Barrier
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Nerf: reduced peak potency ~14% and slightly longer ramp-up.
(Bugfix) Resolved inconsistent trigger interactions reported in live matches (occurrence ~18%).
abilities.description: Arceus conjures a Cosmic Barrier around a target ally, granting them a shield that absorbs damage. The strength of the shield depends on the currently active Elemental Plate. Fire Plate grants a shield that absorbs 150 damage. Water Plate grants a shield that absorbs 100 damage and regenerates 1% max hp per second. Grass Plate grants a shield that absorbs 100 damage and heals the target for 5% max hp upon breaking. Electric Plate grants a shield that absorbs 200 damage. The shield lasts for 4 seconds or until broken and has a cooldown of 12 seconds. The ally must be within a medium range to be targeted.
abilities.flavorQuote: A shield of cosmic energy protects you!

abilities.name: Omnipotent Aura
upgrades: (Bugfix) Resolved inconsistent trigger interactions reported in live matches (occurrence ~38%).
abilities.description: Arceus emanates an Omnipotent Aura for 8 seconds, greatly enhancing the effects of its Elemental Plates. While the aura is active, Fire Plate increases ally attack damage by 25%. Water Plate increases ally magic defense by 25% and grants a minor cleanse removing one debuff every 2 seconds. Grass Plate heals allies for 5% of their maximum HP every second and cleanses allies of burns and poisons every 2 seconds. Electric Plate reduces enemy movement speed by 40% and has a 25% chance to inflict a brief stun (0.5 seconds) with each tick. This ability has a long cooldown of 60 seconds and affects allies and enemies within a large radius.
abilities.flavorQuote: Behold, the power of creation unleashed!

abilities.name: Multitype Adaptation
upgrades: (Bugfix) Resolved inconsistent trigger interactions reported in live matches (occurrence ~17%).
abilities.description: Arceus gains 1% Tenacity and 1% Evasion for each unique type present on the allied team. This bonus caps at 10% Tenacity and 10% Evasion. For example, if the allied team consists of a Fire, Water, and Grass type character alongside Arceus, it will gain 3% Tenacity and 3% Evasion. This passive encourages diverse team compositions, enhancing Arceus's survivability and resistance to crowd control. Should an ally be multi-typed, that only counts as one type for the purposes of this passive.
abilities.flavorQuote: I draw strength from the diversity of creation.

character_v1.playstyle: Reactive Elemental Support
character_v1.teamSynergy: Arceus synergizes well with teams that benefit from constant elemental buffs and debuffs. Characters that can capitalize on attack damage increases, magic defense increases, healing, or slowed enemies will excel alongside Arceus. Its Multitype Adaptation passive encourages team diversity, making it a flexible addition to various team compositions.
character_v1.tierSummary: Arceus's A-Tier support placement is maintained solely by Omnipotent Aura's cleanse and scaling utility; otherwise, Elemental Shift's predictable cycle and Judgment Bolt's limited CC hinder reactive plays. Compared to top-tier supports, Cosmic Barrier's shield offers insufficient burst protection, while Multitype Adaptation provides minimal impact without specific team compositions. Viability hinges on exploiting Aura's burst-heal potential and type-diversity synergy, but its reliance on predictable elemental rotations creates easily exploitable weaknesses; its healing and support output is generally outperformed by higher-tier selections, thus limiting competitive usage.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Arceus's kit revolves around its Elemental Shift passive. Judgment Bolt and Cosmic Barrier actively benefit from this passive by gaining different effects depending on the current plate, creating a dynamic playstyle. Omnipotent Aura amplifies the Elemental Plate effects providing bursts of strong support, while Multitype Adaptation encourages teammates to select a diverse team for more Tenacity/Evasion.

character_v1.name: Eleven

abilities.name: Basic Attack

abilities.name: Telekinetic Barrier
abilities.description: Eleven focuses her psychic energy to create a protective barrier at a target location within a medium range. This barrier absorbs incoming damage, shielding allies within its radius. The barrier's strength scales with Eleven's magic attack. The barrier lasts for a duration of 5 seconds, after which it collapses, releasing a pulse that briefly slows enemies caught within its radius by 30% for 2 seconds. Casting this ability generates 15 Psychic Resonance. The barrier has a health pool equal to 200 + (50% of Eleven's Magic Attack). Subsequent castings will refresh the barrier's duration but do not stack the health pool; any remaining health is retained. This ability has a cooldown of 12 seconds.
abilities.flavorQuote: "I can protect them."

abilities.name: Psychic Push
abilities.description: Eleven unleashes a focused blast of telekinetic energy in a line, pushing enemies back and dealing magic damage. The push distance and damage scale with Eleven's magic attack. Enemies pushed into walls or other solid objects take additional damage equal to 20% of their max HP as True Damage. This ability generates 20 Psychic Resonance. Psychic Push has a medium range. It deals 80 + (40% of Eleven's Magic Attack) magic damage. The cooldown for Psychic Push is 8 seconds. This ability is crucial for controlling enemy positioning and setting up advantageous scenarios for your team, allowing for tactical displacements during engagements.
abilities.flavorQuote: "Get out of my way!"

abilities.name: Sensory Deprivation
abilities.description: Eleven taps into the Void, creating a zone of sensory deprivation at a target location. Enemies within the zone have their vision drastically reduced and their attack speed slowed by 25% for 4 seconds. The zone persists for 6 seconds. Casting Sensory Deprivation generates 10 Psychic Resonance. The range of the zone is medium. While within the zone, enemies also have a 15% chance to miss their attacks entirely. The radius of the Sensory Deprivation zone is significant, affecting multiple enemies simultaneously. This ability has a cooldown of 15 seconds. Sensory Deprivation can be strategically placed to disrupt enemy formations, providing cover for allies or setting up ambushes.
abilities.flavorQuote: "I can't see..."

abilities.name: Psychic Resonance
upgrades: (Bugfix) Resolved inconsistent trigger interactions reported in live matches (occurrence ~28%).
(Bugfix) Resolved inconsistent trigger interactions reported in live matches (occurrence ~47%).
abilities.description: Eleven's abilities generate Psychic Resonance. At 100 Resonance, her next ability becomes Overloaded. Overloaded abilities have increased effects, but after using an Overloaded ability, Eleven becomes Psychically Vulnerable for 5 seconds, taking 20% increased damage from all sources. Overloaded Telekinetic Barrier grants allies within the barrier a 15% increase to their attack damage. Overloaded Psychic Push deals an additional 50% damage and stuns targets for 1.5 seconds. Overloaded Sensory Deprivation silences enemies within the zone for 2 seconds.
abilities.flavorQuote: "I feel... stronger."

abilities.name: Upside Down Collapse
abilities.description: Eleven channels the power of the Upside Down, creating a large zone that pulls enemies towards its center over 3 seconds. At the end of the duration, the zone collapses, dealing massive magic damage to enemies caught within and stunning them for 2 seconds. The damage scales significantly with Eleven's magic attack. This ability generates 30 Psychic Resonance upon cast, regardless of whether it hits enemies. The ultimate has a long range, allowing Eleven to influence engagements from a safe distance. The initial pull effect is gradual but becomes stronger over time, making it difficult for enemies to escape before the final collapse. This ability deals 250 + (80% of Eleven's Magic Attack) magic damage and has a cooldown of 90 seconds.
abilities.flavorQuote: "It's coming..."

character_v1.playstyle: Strategic Battlefield Manipulation with Burst Potential
character_v1.teamSynergy: Eleven pairs well with damage dealers who can capitalize on her crowd control and zone creation. Tanks can benefit from her Telekinetic Barrier, and assassins can utilize her Psychic Push for easy target access.
character_v1.tierSummary: Eleven's S-tier status as a Zone Controller is upheld by her potent Psychic Push/Barrier combo, creating impassable terrain and isolating key targets; however, her reliance on Resonance for overloaded abilities introduces exploitable downtime, demanding precise ability sequencing to maintain pressure. Compared to peers like Blossom, Eleven sacrifices raw damage for superior displacement and denial, positioning her as a reactive, rather than proactive, threat. While Upside Down Collapse offers devastating area control, its long cast time renders it vulnerable to interruption, requiring careful setup and teammate coordination for optimal execution. She fills a strong niche but risks falling off without mastery of Resonance management.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Eleven's kit revolves around controlling the battlefield with zones and displacing enemies, setting up favorable conditions for her team. Her Passive encourages strategic ability usage and awareness of vulnerability windows.

character_v1.name: Jane Margolis

abilities.name: Smoke Break
upgrades: Lv10: +10% ATK Scaling
Lv50: 'Coughing Fit' also reduces target's accuracy by 10%.
Lv100: 'Smoke Break' now heals Jane for 10% of the damage dealt.
mechanics: Applies debuff.
Scales with ATK.
Deals bonus damage against specific debuffs.
abilities.description: Jane flicks a cigarette from her pack, lighting it with a practiced ease. Exhaling a plume of smoke, she targets a single enemy with a calculated puff. This attack deals physical damage equivalent to 30% of Jane's Attack plus a base damage of 10. The smoke itself lingers, applying a 'Coughing Fit' debuff to the target for 1.5 seconds. 'Coughing Fit' reduces the target's attack speed by 15%. Each subsequent 'Smoke Break' attack on the same target increases the duration of the 'Coughing Fit' by 0.25 seconds, up to a maximum of 2.5 seconds. If the target is already affected by the 'Withdrawal' debuff, 'Smoke Break' also deals bonus physical damage equal to 10% of the target's maximum health, ignoring armor. This bonus damage can only occur once every 5 seconds per target.

abilities.name: Blackmail
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
(Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
abilities.description: Jane leverages her knowledge to exploit enemy weaknesses. Target enemy receives a debuff that amplifies damage taken from all sources by 10% + (2% per Withdrawal stack), lasting for 5 seconds. The duration is refreshed each time the affected target is hit by an ally. While this debuff is active, Jane gains vision of the target, ignoring stealth and revealing them on the minimap. If the target dies while Blackmail is active, Jane gains a temporary 20% increase in speed for 3 seconds, representing a fleeting sense of victory. This ability has a cooldown of 8 seconds.
abilities.flavorQuote: I will burn you to the ground.

abilities.name: Relapse
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
abilities.description: Jane succumbs to her addiction, unleashing a wave of debilitating toxins. Jane consumes 5 Withdrawal stacks, dealing 50 + (10 per stack consumed) magic damage to all nearby enemies and inflicting 'Euphoria' for 3 seconds. Euphoria reduces enemy attack speed by 20% and movement speed by 15%. For each enemy affected by Euphoria, Jane heals for 2% of her max HP. After using Relapse, Jane gains 3 stacks of Withdrawal, representing the immediate return of her addiction’s influence. This ability has a cooldown of 12 seconds.
abilities.flavorQuote: I backslid, okay? Like, what? What, you think I'm proud of this?

abilities.name: Apology Girl
upgrades: (Bugfix) Resolved inconsistent trigger interactions reported in live matches (occurrence ~26%).
(Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
abilities.description: Jane's attempts at amends have unintended consequences. Every 10 seconds, Jane generates 1 stack of 'Withdrawal', up to a maximum of 10 stacks. Each stack of Withdrawal increases the potency of her debuffs by a small percentage (see abilities) and restores 1% of her missing health per second. However, each stack of Withdrawal also increases the damage she takes from all sources by 3%, reflecting her growing vulnerability. This passive encourages strategic ability usage to manage Withdrawal stacks for optimal risk/reward.
abilities.flavorQuote: I’m sorry.

abilities.name: Haunted
abilities.description: Jane confronts her inner demons, projecting her guilt onto a single target. Jane spends all stacks of Withdrawal. Target enemy is afflicted with 'Guilt' for 4 seconds. While under the effect of Guilt, the enemy’s healing received is reduced by 30% + (5% per Withdrawal stack spent), and their next damaging ability against an ally is reflected back onto themselves for 50% of the original damage. This reflection cannot trigger critical hits. After using Haunted, Jane is stunned for 0.5 seconds, representing the emotional toll of the ability. Cooldown of 15 seconds.
abilities.flavorQuote: It was me. I killed her, man. I killed her.

abilities.name: Smoke Screen
upgrades: Increased Radius: Expands the reach of Jane's protective smoke, increasing the radius of both the initial shield application and the subsequent debuff by 100 units.
Lingering Haze: Extends the duration of the 'Smoked' debuff, prolonging the enemy's debilitated state by an additional 0.5 seconds.
Fortified Resilience: Reinforces the shield granted to allies, increasing its protective capacity by an additional 10% of Jane's maximum health.
Second-hand Smoke: Imbues the dissipating smoke with an additional effect, applying a 10% slow to all enemies within the area for 2 seconds after the 'Smoked' debuff wears off.
(Balance Patch) Late Bloom: The shielding scales better as the game progresses, making it more effective at later levels.
(Patch) Support Focus: Enhances the supportive aspects of the ability.
abilities.description: With a flick of her wrist, Jane ignites a cigarette, the tendrils of smoke reflecting her turbulent state and, unexpectedly, shielding her companions. Upon activation, Jane exhales a plume of thick smoke, immediately granting herself and all allied heroes within a 600-unit radius the 'Resilience' buff for a duration of 4 seconds. This Resilience provides an immediate shield, absorbing incoming damage equivalent to 20% of Jane's maximum health, offering vital protection in the heat of battle. Furthermore, while Resilience is active, allies benefit from a 25% reduction in damage taken from all sources, mitigating even the most devastating attacks. As the Resilience buff dissipates, the lingering smoke disorients any nearby enemies; all enemy heroes caught within a 400-unit radius are afflicted with the 'Smoked' debuff for 1.5 seconds, reducing their attack damage by 30% and their movement speed by 20%. Smoke Screen has a cooldown of 75 seconds.

character_v1.playstyle: Debuff Support/Damage Amplifier
character_v1.teamSynergy: Jane excels in teams that can capitalize on her amplified damage and debuffs. Characters with high burst damage or consistent damage output benefit greatly from Blackmail. Tanks can protect her from the increased vulnerability caused by Withdrawal. Her slows from Choke on It enable allies to easily land skillshots or engage in prolonged fights.
character_v1.tierSummary: Jane Margolis' kit, while thematically resonant, suffers from fractured synergy, relegating her to mid-tier viability. 'Blackmail' offers crucial vision and damage amplification, but its value is undermined by 'Relapse' and 'Haunted,' abilities that demand contradictory stack management of 'Apology Girl.' Compared to A-tier peers like Puss in Boots and Trunks, Jane lacks consistent control or focused support, making her a suboptimal pick. 'Choke on It' provides brief invulnerability and potential burst, but its dependence on setup and team coordination limits reliable application, reducing her overall impact. The lack of cohesive strategy makes her toolkit clunky.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Jane's kit revolves around managing her Withdrawal stacks to amplify her debuffs, but at the cost of increased vulnerability. Relapse allows her to consume stacks for damage and healing, while Haunted spends them for powerful debuffs and reflect. Blackmail provides utility through vision and damage amplification, while her ultimate offers a brief burst of power at a significant personal cost.

abilities.flavorQuote: "Mordecai and Rigby! Get back to work!"

abilities.name: Overtime!
abilities.description: Benson forces an ally into 'Overtime', granting them 20% increased attack speed and movement speed for 4 seconds. This ability also grants the ally a shield equal to 10% of Benson's Max HP that lasts for 4 seconds. This ability generates 15 Stress. If Benson's Stress Gauge is above 50%, the attack and movement speed bonus is increased to 30%. If Benson’s Stress Gauge reaches 100% after using this ability, instead of buffing the ally, Benson consumes all stress and shields himself for 25% of his max HP.
abilities.flavorQuote: "You two! Work harder, or you're fired!"

abilities.name: Managerial Outburst
upgrades: Reduce stress penalty upon reaching 100 stress.
abilities.description: Benson, overcome by the sheer incompetence surrounding him, unleashes a torrent of pent-up frustration. He surges forward a short distance, propelled by pure, unadulterated managerial stress. During this short dash, lasting 2 seconds, Benson's built-in gumball dispensers go into overdrive, firing a cone of sticky projectiles at all enemies in front of him. Each gumball inflicts X physical damage upon impact, with a maximum of 10 gumballs able to strike a single target during the fit. The sheer act of expelling this much sugary ammunition generates 20 Stress within Benson, bringing him closer to his boiling point. Should Benson's Stress Gauge already be above 50% prior to unleashing this tirade, the force behind the gumballs becomes amplified, causing enemies struck to be knocked back a short distance, effectively disrupting their formations and potentially interrupting any abilities they were attempting to use. If Benson's Stress Gauge reaches 100% as a direct result of the Managerial Outburst, he enters a state of blind, furious resilience. For the duration of the 2-second gumball barrage, Benson becomes temporarily immune to all forms of damage, shrugging off attacks that would normally halt his advance. However, this enraged state also significantly impairs his movement speed, reducing it by 50%, rendering him a relatively stationary target amidst the chaos.

abilities.name: Getting Too Stressed! (Passive)
upgrades: [object Object]
[object Object]
[object Object]
(Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
abilities.description: Benson, ever the diligent manager, is prone to overwork and subsequent stress. Each time an ally unleashes an ability within a generous radius of Benson, his Stress Meter inflates by 5 units, reflecting his concern for operational efficiency. Furthermore, as his own health dwindles, the pressure mounts; for every 5% of Benson's maximum health he loses, the Stress Meter climbs another 10 units. When the pressure becomes unbearable and the Stress Meter maxes out at 100, Benson experiences a momentary but debilitating 'Meltdown'. During this 2-second meltdown phase, Benson is rendered stunned, his focus shattered, leaving him vulnerable to enemy attacks. Upon the meltdown's abrupt conclusion, the Stress Meter is immediately purged back to 0, giving Benson a chance to recover his composure. As a further measure of self-preservation, while Benson teeters below 30% of his maximum health, his inherent desire to stay on top of things compels him to absorb healing effects more efficiently, increasing the potency of all incoming healing by a significant 20%, helping him push through the deadline and maintain his composure.

abilities.name: YOU'RE FIRED!!! (Ultimate)
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Late Game Buff: Ability scaling improved — Gaining extra power at later levels.
(Patch) Role Realignment: ability now emphasizes damage-style interactions.
abilities.description: Benson slams his fist down on his gumball machine, unleashing a wave of pure managerial frustration. This manifests as a devastating verbal barrage, dealing X Magic Damage to all enemies across the battlefield. In addition, Benson's righteous fury empowers his allies, granting them a 20% increase to their damage output for a base duration of 6 seconds. This ability consumes all of Benson's accumulated Stress. For every 20 Stress consumed in the process, the duration of the damage buff is extended by 1 second, up to a maximum of 10 seconds. Thus, if Benson unleashes this ability with 80 Stress accumulated, his allies' damage is amplified for the full 10 seconds. Moreover, if Benson is in 'Breakdown' status when activating 'YOU'RE FIRED!!!', the initial magic damage dealt to enemies is boosted by 50%, turning his managerial displeasure into a truly devastating force of nature.

character_v1.playstyle: Risk/Reward Stress Accumulator
character_v1.teamSynergy: Benson synergizes well with teams that have high ability usage, as this rapidly fills his Stress Gauge, allowing him to use enhanced abilities more frequently. He also benefits from healers who can keep him alive long enough to reach high stress levels and capitalize on the increased damage and effects. Characters that can grant temporary invulnerability or cleanse stuns are valuable to mitigate the 'Breakdown' state.
character_v1.tierSummary: Benson's A-tier placement hinges on his potent 'Overtime!' buff and ultimate, 'Legendary Drum Solo', providing valuable utility and AoE damage, respectively. However, his role as a utility character is diluted by his reliance on a stress mechanic that is neither reliably controllable nor offers consistently impactful payoff through 'Stress Management (Passive)'. Compared to other A-tier controllers like Puss in Boots, Benson's kit lacks the decisive control options necessary to consistently dictate the flow of battle. His 'Raging Reprimand' offers limited debuffing potential, failing to secure his position against more impactful support and controller peers in the meta. Ultimately, Benson is a mid-tier character carried by specific buffing capacity and hindered by an under-tuned passive and limited control utility relative to peers.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Benson's kit revolves around the Stress Gauge. His abilities build stress, enhancing their effects, but too much stress leads to Breakdown. Players must balance stress generation with the power of his abilities and be mindful of Breakdown. 'Stress Management' makes him a potent late-game tank, while the ultimate rewards smart stress-stacking.

character_v1.teamSynergy: Maddie synergizes well with teams that can benefit from zone control and damage amplification, as well as those who can take advantage of her barrier placement to create opportunities.
character_v1.tierSummary: Maddie's zone control, while potent on paper via 'Fenton Barrier Grid' and 'Ecto-Pulse Mine,' suffers from setup reliance and limited reactive options, making her predictable compared to higher-tier controllers. Her 'Ectoplasmic Intuition' scaling is insufficient to justify her lack of immediate impact, especially when competing with established A-tier peers who offer more consistent utility. Viability hinges on chaining 'Fenton Barrier Grid' with 'Ecto-Pulse Mine' for guaranteed trap hits, but this is easily countered with awareness. 'Spectral Frequency Modulator' provides niche magic defense but is generally outclassed. 'Ghost Shield Gauntlet' is her only real defensive tool, but it's insufficient for a character so vulnerable to dives.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Maddie's kit is designed around applying 'Ecto-Resonance' and then capitalizing on it with her other abilities, creating amplified effects and increased damage output.

abilities.description: Don-chan channels his boundless Taiko spirit into a life-saving rhythm for his allies. When activated, a series of four commands appears, each demanding either a resounding 'Don!' or a sharp 'Ka!' to match the beat. Successfully executing this musical sequence sends a surge of restorative energy to the targeted ally, mending their wounds and returning vigor, instantly healing them for a robust 15% of their maximum health pool. As the rhythmic healing takes effect, a protective aura forms around the recipient, a shimmering shield that absorbs incoming damage equal to 10% of Don-chan's own potent magic attack, safeguarding them from harm for a crucial 3 seconds. This protective shield is invaluable in weathering incoming attacks, offering a buffer against the enemy's onslaught. However, should the player falter, inputting one or more incorrect beats during the sequence, the restorative power weakens. The heal diminishes to a still-helpful 7.5% of the target's maximum health, and the shield's strength decreases to only 5% of Don-chan's magic attack. Moreover, its duration is halved, lasting for only 1.5 seconds, a fleeting defense against immediate danger. Drumming Benediction demands concentration and rhythmic precision, as it comes with a cooldown of 8 seconds, demanding careful management and well-timed execution for maximum impact on the battlefield.

Upon activation, Don-chan must successfully perform a sequence of six 'Don' or 'Ka' inputs within a tight 3-second window. Each successful input resonates outwards, weakening the resolve of enemies caught in the barrage's wake. Each successful input reduces the attack speed and movement speed of enemies within the affected area by a palpable 8% for a duration of 4 seconds; these effects stack additively, intensifying the rhythmic oppression with each perfectly timed strike. However, any incorrect input shatters the rhythmic flow, instantly resetting the debuff duration and demanding unwavering precision to maintain the cacophony of disruption. Should Don-chan flawlessly execute all six inputs, enemies are not only slowed but also afflicted with 'Rhythm Break,' a profound disruption that reduces their tenacity by a substantial 20% for the full duration of the barrage. Drumbeat Barrage has a 12-second cooldown, requiring strategic timing to effectively cripple enemy formations and exploit vulnerabilities exposed by rhythmic discord.

character_v1.playstyle: Rhythm-based Support
character_v1.teamSynergy: Don-chan pairs well with damage-focused allies who benefit from increased attack damage and speed. His abilities provide both offensive and defensive support, making him a versatile addition to any team composition. Characters with high burst damage can benefit significantly from the 'Rhythmic Surge' buff, while those who rely on sustained damage can utilize the lifesteal provided by 'Sonic Symphony.'
character_v1.tierSummary: Don-Chan's reliance on 'Rhythm Resonance' for meaningful buffs and debuffs makes his kit inconsistent and easily countered, diminishing his buffer role. His single-target basic attack is underwhelming given the prevalence of AoE damage dealers, and his ultimate, while potent, is gated behind a rhythm mechanic vulnerable to disruption. Compared to other B-tier supports, Don-Chan's buff uptime and reliability are demonstrably lower, hindering his competitive viability. The 'Drumbeat Dynamo' and 'Sonic Symphony' combination represents his theoretical peak, but its practical application is severely limited by the rhythm gate. Ultimately, Don-Chan's kit lacks the consistent, impactful utility necessary to justify his selection in a competitive environment.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Don-chan's abilities are designed to synergize by rewarding accurate rhythm inputs. The passive ability 'Drumbeat Dynamo' enhances allies after successful sequences, while 'Tempo Tantrum' can disrupt enemies, creating opportunities for allies to capitalize on the chaos. 'Precision Performance' makes all other abilities slightly easier to perform. 'Sonic Symphony' can both buff allies and debuff enemies at the same time if performed correctly.

character_v1.playstyle: Combo-focused melee fighter who gains power from nearby allies and excels at protecting them.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Tatsuki synergizes well with teams that have auras or can consistently provide buffs to allies, maximizing the benefits of her 'Aura Echo' mechanic. character_v1.tierSummary: Tatsuki's S-tier bruiser status hinges on potent stat-scaling, particularly speed and defense, amplified by 'Aura Echo' across key abilities. 'Guardian's Stance' and 'Unwavering Protector' grant substantial defense and utility, but their effectiveness is conditional. While her kit offers good self-sustain and ally support, she's outclassed in raw damage compared to top-tier bruisers like Omniman and lacks the oppressive control of characters like Tao, rendering her dependent on specific team compositions to maintain viability despite favorable matchups.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Tatsuki's kit revolves around her ability to amplify her abilities through proximity to allies and to protect them when they are in danger, creating a synergy between her damage output and supportive capabilities.

His reliance on Machete Swing for damage and Grasping Terror for initiation is telegraphed, making him vulnerable to zoning and burst. Compared to S-tier bruisers like Li, Tatsuki, and even Omniman on top tier, Jason lacks consistent, reliable damage output and is heavily reliant on landing key stuns, a significant weakness against faster, more mobile characters. Unyielding Stalker's short duration provides insufficient disruption or damage mitigation, while Crystal Lake's Fury's reliance on cleave damage proves less impactful than other bruisers with guaranteed burst options, relegating him to mid-tier viability at best within the context of the broader S-tier population.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Jason's kit revolves around building 'Camp Dread' through damage taken and crowd control, empowering his abilities and basic attacks. 'Relentless Pursuit' fuels his enraged state, while 'Machete Swing' and 'Grasping Terror' quickly generate stacks. 'Unyielding Stalker' allows for aggressive engagements and 'Crystal Lake's Fury' unleashes devastating damage and area control.

abilities.description: Trunks focuses his Saiyan power, drawing on his experience in the Hyperbolic Time Chamber to unleash a devastating assault. While under the effect of 'Burning Attack Unleashed', each of Trunks' sword attacks cleaves through enemies, inflicting additional true damage equal to 20% of his attack damage plus an additional flat amount based on his current level. Moreover, each successful strike carries a 30% chance to stun the target for a brief 0.75 seconds, leaving them vulnerable to further attacks. The immense power surge also generates a protective shield around Trunks, absorbing incoming damage equal to 150% of his attack damage throughout the duration of 'Burning Attack Unleashed'. This shield decays rapidly after 5 seconds. Once the 'Burning Attack Unleashed' status expires, Trunks channels the residual energy into his sword, increasing his attack damage by 15% for the subsequent 5 seconds, allowing for a final surge of offensive capability. This ability requires a considerable amount of Ki to activate and has a long cooldown to reflect the intensity of the transformation.

character_v1.playstyle: Burst Damage Support
character_v1.teamSynergy: Trunks provides strong burst damage potential and some utility through stuns and speed boosts. He synergizes well with teams that can capitalize on brief windows of opportunity or require a damage amplifier.
character_v1.tierSummary: Trunks' A-tier support placement is questionable; his kit lacks cohesive synergy compared to peers. 'Burning Stance' provides minimal value, failing to offer impactful protection for allies or significant self-sustain despite its scaling. 'Temporal Shift' offers brief escape utility but doesn't reliably enable team plays; it is outpaced by dedicated controllers and supports. 'Shining Sword Slash' is a niche burst option that poorly complements his supposed support role, creating split focus. His viability hinges almost entirely on 'Saiyan Lineage' augmenting his meager stats; absent significant external buffs, he's easily outclassed by more specialized units.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Trunks' kit is designed to empower his sword attacks through Temporal Surge. 'Saiyan Lineage' extends the duration of Temporal Surge, while 'Shining Sword Slash' benefits directly from its effects. 'Burning Attack' sets up enemies for increased sword damage.

character_v1.tierSummary: Android 18 excels in zone control, leveraging 'Destructo-Disc Field' to create persistent, damaging zones that synergize with 'Android Agility' for aggressive zoning and evasive maneuvers; 'Endless Energy' sustains her aggression, outlasting many similarly-ranked characters; however, her reliance on field placement makes her susceptible to characters with strong displacement or burst mobility; compared to top-tier controllers, her immediate crowd control is limited, positioning her slightly below the absolute meta.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Android 18's kit revolves around controlling space with her Energy Fields. Her abilities are designed to punish enemies who either ignore or destroy her fields, while simultaneously providing utility and buffs to her allies. Her passive ensures she remains a constant threat, even under pressure.

Should Frieza's Golden form be active, these energy spheres transcend their limitations, piercing through the first enemy they strike and continuing to obliterate any unfortunate soul caught within the volley's path.
