abilities.description: Unleash a devastating volley of miniature, super-compressed energy spheres, each a shimmering testament to Frieza's refined cruelty and mastery over Ki manipulation. Instead of a singular strike, Frieza rapidly generates and launches a multitude of these 'Death Comets' at a single target with unnerving precision. These projectiles, rather than impacting simultaneously, strike in rapid succession over a brief period of roughly one and a half seconds, creating a localized zone of chaotic energy bombardment. Each comet deals a moderate amount of physical damage, scaling primarily with Frieza's ATK stat and benefitting from critical hit chance and damage modifiers. However, the true strength of Death Comet Barrage lies in its persistent debuff application. Each successful hit from a Death Comet applies a stack of 'Ki Suppression' to the target. Each stack reduces the target's Ki regeneration rate by a small percentage (stacking multiplicatively to a maximum cap). Upon reaching a certain number of Ki Suppression stacks, the target suffers a brief period of 'Ki Disruption,' significantly increasing the cooldown of their next ability cast. Therefore, Death Comet Barrage is not merely a damage tool, but a tactical instrument designed to disrupt enemy combos, limit their offensive capabilities, and starve them of resources within Frieza's controlled zone, leaving them vulnerable to follow-up attacks and further exploitation. It's a display of overwhelming force disguised as a seemingly simple barrage, epitomizing Frieza's approach to combat: calculated, relentless, and utterly demoralizing. This ability reflects the visual of a golden aura surrounding the hand as small purple orbs are created and fired. After a moment, the ability goes on a moderate cooldown.
abilities.flavorQuote: Such a dazzling display of destruction, isn't it? Pity you're on the receiving end.

abilities.name: Planet Crushing Ball
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
abilities.description: Frieza charges a massive energy sphere for 1.75 seconds (can be interrupted), which upon release, deals significant magic damage to a targeted area. The damage is increased by 1% for every 2 'Oppression' stacks Frieza possesses upon casting. Enemies at the center of the blast take 25% increased damage and are knocked back a moderate distance. This ability has a long cooldown. If Frieza is in Golden Form, this attack becomes instant cast and deals true damage equal to 10% of the target's current HP in addition to the magic damage.
abilities.flavorQuote: Say goodbye to your insignificant world!

abilities.name: My Golden Form!
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Nerf: reduced peak potency ~17% and slightly longer ramp-up.
(Bugfix) Resolved inconsistent trigger interactions reported in live matches (occurrence ~41%).
abilities.description: When the measure of Frieza's dominance, represented by 100 stacks of Oppression, is full, he can unleash his ultimate evolution, declaring to the lesser beings that he will show them his 'Golden Form!' For 10 glorious seconds, Frieza transcends his previous limitations. Initially, the transformation grants Frieza a brief invulnerability, a shimmering golden aura protecting him from all harm for 1.5 seconds, a testament to his absolute power. In this radiant state, Frieza's attacks strike with increased ferocity, his attack damage soaring by 25%, demonstrating the true extent of his evolved strength. Moreover, during the Golden Form, each of Frieza's abilities are augmented with additional, devastating effects. However, such power comes at a price. As the Golden Form fades, Frieza's body is wracked with 'Exhaustion', his speed and attack damage reduced by 15% for 5 seconds, a humbling reminder of his mortal coil. This ability has a very long cooldown.

abilities.name: Tyranny
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Tyranny's reach diminished: Peak potency reduced by approximately 12%, with a slightly extended ramp-up time to achieve maximum effect.
(Balance Patch) Buff: ability scale improved — gains extra potency at late levels.
(Bugfix) Resolved inconsistent trigger interactions reported in live matches (occurrence ~27%).
abilities.description: Frieza exudes an aura of absolute Tyranny, crushing the spirits of his foes and solidifying his dominance. Whenever Frieza inflicts a debuff upon an enemy champion, whether it be a slow, stun, or any other form of impairment, he gains 5 stacks of 'Tyranny', representing his tightening grip on the battlefield. Further demonstrating his overwhelming power, Frieza's basic attacks have a 20% chance to apply 'Suppression' to his target. 'Suppression' weakens the target, reducing their outgoing damage by 10% for a duration of 2 seconds, a period during which they are forced to endure Frieza's might. This 'Suppression' effect does not stack, preventing enemies from being completely nullified. Each critical strike Frieza lands grants him a burst of power, awarding him 2 additional stacks of 'Tyranny'. Finally, to cement his unwavering control, Frieza gains increased tenacity based on his stacks of 'Tyranny'. For every 10 stacks he accumulates, his tenacity is increased by 1%, with a maximum possible increase of 10% tenacity, representing his near-unbreakable will.

character_v1.playstyle: Punishing aggressors and controlling space through debuffs and calculated bursts of power with Golden Frieza transformation.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Frieza synergizes well with team compositions that can amplify his zone control or provide crowd control to set up his Planet Crushing Ball. Allies that can apply additional debuffs or peel for him during the Exhaustion phase after Golden Form are highly beneficial. Frieza also benefits from allies who can capitalize on the increased damage vulnerability inflicted by his 'Fragile' debuff during his Golden form.
character_v1.tierSummary: Frieza's oppressive zoning kit, defined by 'Death Beam Barrage' and 'Planet Crushing Ball', allows unmatched area control; however, the reliance on 'Oppression' stacks for 'My Golden Form!' introduces a critical vulnerability to tenacity-stacking compositions. Compared to fellow S-tiers like Android 18 and other zone control specialists, Frieza's delayed burst and interruptible nuke telegraphs his intentions, creating counterplay windows. This predictability, combined with the current meta favoring high-mobility assassins like Tao and Omniman, who can bypass his zoning, limits his overall effectiveness despite raw damage output. Therefore, while his theoretical damage is high, practical application requires careful positioning and team support to mitigate his clear weaknesses in the current landscape.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Frieza's kit revolves around building Oppression stacks quickly through debuffs and damage. The core gameplay loop involves using Death Beam Barrage and Emperor's Pressure to debuff enemies, generating Oppression, and then unleashing the Planet Crushing Ball for significant damage. Golden Tyrant provides a temporary window for enhanced damage output and invulnerability, rewarding aggressive plays and punishing enemies who engage him during this phase.

Additionally, when Tao's shield is broken, she gains 15% increased evasion for 3 seconds. Her base tenacity is increased by 10 and her base evasion is increased by 5. This signature passive provides Tao with additional sustain and survivability, allowing her to stay in the fight longer and recover from critical hits, enhancing her role as a resilient assassin capable of trading blows effectively.

character_v1.playstyle: Tao is designed as a high-risk, high-reward assassin that uses ammo consumption to power up her abilities and deliver devastating burst damage. Her kit revolves around stacking Blade Heart through aggressive play, then capitalizing on those stacks to enhance her Swords Out and Fatal Bloom skills. This requires precise timing and resource management to maximize her effectiveness in combat.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Tao excels in teams that can provide sustained damage and crowd control, allowing her to focus on eliminating high-priority targets. Allies that can buff her attack and magic attack further amplify her burst potential, while those that can provide shields can help her maintain Blade Heart stacks more consistently.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Tao's abilities are heavily intertwined through the Blade Heart mechanic. Consuming ammo feeds into Blade Heart stacks, which amplify her damage output with Swords Out and Fatal Bloom. The ultimate provides an explosive release of her accumulated Blade Heart, incentivizing aggressive play and resource management.

abilities.description: Crown Prince throws a Smoke Grenade at the targeted location, creating a cloud of smoke with a 4-meter radius. Enemies within the smoke cloud are blinded for 2 seconds, reducing their accuracy by 50%. The smoke also applies a stacking Corrosion effect that deals 10 (+5% Magic Atk) magic damage per second for 4 seconds. This Corrosion damage increases by 20% for each stack, up to a maximum of 3 stacks. The Smoke Grenade lasts for 6 seconds, and the ability has a cooldown of 12 seconds. This ability targets a ground location.

upgrades: Level 40: Additional damage increased to 30% when two or more elemental effects are present.
Level 90: Also grants 10% increased magic attack when two or more elemental effects are present.

Level 190: When three or more elemental effects are present, the bonus damage and magic attack are doubled.
abilities.description: Crown Prince possesses a deep understanding of elemental interactions. Whenever an enemy is affected by two or more unique elemental effects (e.g., Decay and Corrosion), Crown Prince's basic attacks and abilities deal an additional 20% magic damage to that enemy. Additionally, Crown Prince gains 10% increased shield regeneration rate. This passive constantly monitors the status effects on enemies.

upgrades: Level 150: Damage increased to 300 (+120% Magic Atk).
Level 200: Cooldown reduced to 60 seconds, and the cone area is widened by 20%.
abilities.description: Crown Prince channels the power of the Spirit Realm, unleashing a wave of elemental energy in a cone-shaped area in front of him. This wave deals 200 (+80% Magic Atk) magic damage and applies all available elemental effects (Decay, Corrosion, Burn, Shock, Freeze) to all enemies within the area for 5 seconds. Furthermore, enemies affected by this ability take 30% increased damage from all sources for the duration. This ability has a cooldown of 90 seconds and prioritizes enemies within the cone.

abilities.name: Alchemical Resilience
upgrades: Level 125: Tenacity increased to 45 and debuff cleanse chance increased to 35%.
Level 175: Elemental effects applied by Crown Prince have a 10% chance to also inflict a stacking 'Weakened' debuff, reducing the target's armor and magic resistance by 5% per stack (max 3 stacks).
abilities.description: Crown Prince's alchemical prowess grants him enhanced resilience. He gains 30 Tenacity, reducing the duration of incoming crowd control effects by 30%. Additionally, whenever Crown Prince applies an elemental effect to an enemy, he has a 25% chance to cleanse one random debuff from himself. This effect can only occur once every 8 seconds. Furthermore Crown Prince's base magic resistance is increased by 15.

character_v1.playstyle: Crown Prince is designed as a utility-focused character who excels at enabling elemental damage for his team. While he can deal damage himself, his primary function is to apply Decay and other elemental statuses, amplifying the damage output of allies who can capitalize on these effects.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Crown Prince excels in teams that can capitalize on elemental effects. His ability to apply Decay, Corrosion, and other elemental statuses makes him a valuable asset to any team composition that includes characters with elemental damage or abilities that synergize with status effects. The increased damage vulnerability from Spirit Realm Purification benefits the entire team, allowing for coordinated bursts of damage.
character_v1.internalSynergy: The kit revolves around applying multiple elemental effects to enemies using Energy Orb Barrage and Smoke Grenade Deployment, which then synergizes with Elemental Attunement to increase Crown Prince's damage output. Spirit Realm Purification serves as a powerful ultimate, applying all elemental effects and significantly increasing damage vulnerability, setting up enemies for massive burst damage from Crown Prince and his team.

character_v1.playstyle: Li's kit heavily emphasizes applying and benefiting from the 'Burning' status effect, allowing her to serve as a Fire-damage-focused bruiser. character_v1.teamSynergy: Li synergizes well with other fire-based characters who can consistently apply 'Burning' to enemies, allowing her to quickly build 'Scorched Earth' stacks and maximize her damage output. character_v1.internalSynergy: Li's kit revolves around building and maintaining 'Scorched Earth' stacks by applying 'Burning' to enemies, which then empowers her 'Spiritual Flame' and 'Blazing Meteor' abilities. 'Flame Talisman' offers defensive utility by consuming stacks for damage reduction, while 'Crimson Nova' expends all stacks for a burst of damage and self-buffs, creating a risk-reward playstyle.

abilities.description: Richard, with a barely perceptible shift in his stoic expression, designates a target area for a concentrated bombardment of LEGO studs. These hard plastic projectiles descend upon the marked zone, dealing a total of 80 magic damage, enhanced by 60% of Richard's magic attack power, to any unfortunate enemies caught within the circular zone over a duration of 3 seconds. The area targeted is intelligently selected, prioritizing locations where enemy presence is most dense, ensuring maximum impact. The damage unfolds in a series of rapid ticks, granting enemies fleeting moments to evade the full brunt of the stud storm. Should Richard possess a Royal Decree exceeding 50, the studs are imbued with a binding adhesive, inflicting 'Bricked' upon impact, hindering enemy movement by reducing their speed by 25% for 2 seconds, simulating the frustrating experience of stepping on a LEGO brick. Furthermore, each activation of Stud Barrage replenishes Richard's strategic reserves, granting him 10 Royal Decree. This ability operates on a 10-second cooldown, allowing for calculated deployment in the heat of battle.

abilities.description: Richard, with a world-weary sigh, proclaims a dryly worded Royal Decree, bolstering the ally currently struggling the most. He bestows upon this ally a protective shield, absorbing damage equal to 15% of Richard's maximum health for a duration of 4 seconds. This decree echoes with the authority of Unikingdom, provided Richard's Royal Decree is high enough; if Richard currently possesses more than 50 Royal Decree, the shielded ally also benefits from a 15% increase in their attack power for the shield's duration. This ability operates on a 12-second cooldown. The shield's effectiveness diminishes gradually, decaying by 25% of its original value each second. Only one Royal Decree shield can be active on an ally at any given time; should a new shield be applied, it overwrites the previous one. The sheer monotony of Richard's decree is strangely distracting, causing enemies to momentarily falter, granting all allies a 5% evasion buff for 2 seconds following the shield's application. Furthermore, the act of proclaiming the decree grants Richard 15 Royal Decree.

Allies within the area gain 'Orderly Focus', increasing their atk speed by 25% and reducing their cooldowns by 10%. The area of effect is a large square. This ability has a 90-second cooldown. Richard consumes all Royal Decree upon casting this ability. Enemies and allies entering or exiting the area are immediately affected by the respective status effects. The Time-Out Corner provides a significant advantage in team fights, disrupting enemy formations and empowering allies.

character_v1.playstyle: Richard excels at providing utility and control by buffing allies with 'Rules' and hindering enemies with 'Chores'. His kit revolves around managing Royal Decree to enhance his support capabilities and maintain order on the battlefield, embodying his role as Unikitty's royal advisor.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Richard synergizes well with teams that benefit from atk speed buffs and defensive support. His shields and Def aura provide crucial protection, while his debuffs can disrupt enemy formations and reduce their damage output. He is particularly effective with damage-focused allies who can capitalize on the increased atk speed provided by his ultimate.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Richard's kit synergizes around managing Royal Decree, which enhances his abilities to either buff allies or debuff enemies. His passive ability to gain Royal Decree when allies are affected by negative status effects allows him to consistently empower his abilities. His ultimate consumes Royal Decree to create a powerful zoning effect, further amplifying his support capabilities.

abilities.description: Frantic Flourish is a spectacle of accidental tanking. Upon activation, Tom initiates a series of exaggerated, seemingly panicked movements—a chaotic dance designed to both protect allies and disrupt enemies. During the Flourish, Tom's evasion stat receives a significant boost, allowing him to dodge incoming attacks with surprising (and wholly unintentional) grace. More than that, the sheer unpredictability of Tom's Flourish applies the 'Distracted' debuff, reducing the target's damage output and focus. Visually, expect flailing limbs, cartoonish dust clouds, and perhaps even a misplaced piano key or two. The duration of the evasion buff and the effectiveness of the distraction status is calculated through scaling factors tied to Tom's DEF and HP, improving its overall utility as the character grows.
abilities.flavorQuote: I'm not panicking, you're panicking!

abilities.description: Tom spends 2 seconds building a complex Rube Goldberg machine. During this time, he's immune to crowd control but takes 25% increased damage. Then, a giant magnet activates for 2 seconds, pulling enemies towards the center. Finally, a massive explosion occurs, dealing 300 + (0.6 * X) magic damage in the center and knocking enemies upwards. If Tom has max stacks of 'Cartoon Physics' when activating this ability, the machine also dispenses a random buff to allies within the rain zone, either granting a 25% damage boost or a 20% movement speed increase for 5 seconds.

abilities.name: Cartoon Resilience: The Slapstick Savior

abilities.description: Tom's inherent cartoon logic grants him increased durability. He gains 50 bonus Def and 30 bonus Magic Def. During 'Cartoon Recovery', Tom becomes invulnerable for 1 second, gains 25% increased movement speed, and his tenacity is doubled. This effect has a 60-second cooldown. For each stack of 'Cartoon Physics' Tom possesses at the time 'Cartoon Recovery' triggers, the invulnerability duration is increased by 0.2 seconds, and the cooldown is reduced by 2 seconds. Also, he gains 10 base tenacity.

character_v1.playstyle: Tom is a disruptive tank who thrives in the middle of chaos, using his cartoonish resilience to draw enemy fire and set up opportunities for his team. He's best played aggressively, constantly moving and forcing enemies to react to his unpredictable antics.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Tom excels at disrupting enemy formations and providing temporary openings for his team. He pairs well with damage dealers who can capitalize on his knockbacks and stuns, as well as supports who can keep him alive while he accumulates 'Cartoon Physics' stacks.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Tom's kit is designed to synergize around 'Cartoon Physics'. Getting hit empowers his Mallet Mayhem, strengthens his traps, and enhances his ultimate. The passive provides sustain and escape, while the ultimate provides high-impact AoE disruption.

abilities.description: Jerry's natural agility grants him a 15% bonus to his speed and a 10% chance to evade incoming basic attacks. This item will be one of the following, chosen at random: Cheese, Mallet, Miracle-Gro or Firecracker. This passive ability provides Jerry with increased survivability and resources, allowing him to continuously disrupt and support his team. Prioritize positioning Jerry near trap zones to maximize the item acquisition rate. These items persist until used. He can hold a maximum of 3 Acquired Items at any time; further procs are lost if full.

abilities.description: Jerry unleashes a chaotic flurry of distractions, targeting a large area around him. For 8 seconds, enemies within the area are periodically affected by random status effects: 40% chance to be Charmed for 1 second, 30% chance to be Slowed by 50% for 2 seconds, and a 30% chance to be Blinded for 1 second. Allies within the area gain 20% increased speed and 10% increased damage. This ability has a long cooldown of 90 seconds. Prioritize using Mouse Mayhem in the middle of team fights to maximize disruption and buff potential. The speed buff stacks multiplicatively with Jerry's passive. Each application of a debuff is independent of the others.

abilities.name: Unseen Agility: Mouse Reflexes and Tenacity
upgrades: Level 85: Increases evasion bonus to 35 and tenacity bonus to 25.

Level 200: Jerry's tenacity reduces damage taken from status effects by an additional 10%.
abilities.description: Jerry's inherent agility grants him a permanent increase of 25 to his base evasion and 15 to his base tenacity stats, making him harder to hit and more resistant to crowd control effects. Whenever Jerry successfully evades an attack, his next 'Spring-Loaded Surprise' trap placement is instant and costs no mana/energy. This effect lasts for 5 seconds. This ability directly improves Jerry's survivability and ability to chain traps, allowing him to maintain battlefield control more effectively. Prioritize building additional tenacity to further reduce the duration of crowd control effects. Note that the free trap placement does not stack.

character_v1.playstyle: Jerry is designed as a versatile utility character, focusing on battlefield control, item manipulation, and opportunistic disruption. He uses traps and acquired items to hinder enemies and empower allies, requiring careful planning and resource management.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Jerry excels in teams that can capitalize on enemy displacement and crowd control. His traps and items can set up opportunities for burst damage dealers, while his ultimate ability can disrupt enemy formations and provide buffs to allies, enhancing overall team effectiveness.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Jerry's kit is designed around trap placement and item usage. The passive ability provides a continuous source of items, which can then be used with the active ability. The ultimate ability provides a wide-area distraction, creating opportunities for trap placement and item usage.

character_v1.playstyle: Kakashi is a versatile Adaptive Specialist, excelling at disrupting enemy formations and copying key enemy abilities to turn the tide of battle. He thrives in prolonged engagements, gaining power as he analyzes his opponents and adapts his strategies.

character_v1.internalSynergy: Kakashi's kit revolves around building up Copy Charges to empower his ninjutsu. The passive grants a strong sense of adaptability, while Kamui Raid offers burst damage and disruption. The signature passive reinforces his role as a resilient and adaptive combatant.

abilities.description: Buttercup channels her unparalleled fury into a devastating whirlwind of motion, becoming a nigh-unstoppable force of pure, green-tinged aggression! Upon activation, Buttercup rapidly transforms into a tightly coiled, emerald blur and launches herself forward a moderate distance, leaving a shimmering green afterimage in her wake. During this period of frenzied motion, she becomes momentarily immune to crowd control effects, shrugging off attempts to impede her destructive path with a contemptuous snarl. Any enemy foolish enough to stand in her way is subjected to a relentless barrage of bone-jarring impacts, each strike dealing a calculated amount of physical damage that scales multiplicatively with Buttercup's raw ATK and her current Fury level. Moreover, each successful hit has a chance to inflict a short-duration stacking debuff which lowers their total defense, making them increasingly vulnerable to subsequent attacks. At the end of the roll, or upon colliding with an unyielding obstacle, Buttercup erupts from her green shell, unleashing a concussive shockwave that knocks back nearby enemies. This ability also generates a modest amount of Fury, fueling her other abilities and amplifying her overall combat prowess, embodying her signature impetuousness and sheer, unadulterated power. But beware, this move leaves her briefly vulnerable at the tail end!

abilities.description: Spectral Static—a passive ability that reflects Skulker's aptitude for manipulating ethereal energies. It causes his very presence to emanate a localized field of disruptive energy, clinging to enemies like spectral grime. Specifically, each time Skulker is struck by a melee attack, he passively afflicts the attacker with a stack of 'Static Cling'—an invisible debuff that accumulates until a threshold is reached. Once an enemy accumulates three stacks of 'Static Cling', they are subjected to a brief 'Static Shock'. This shock inflicts a small burst of AoE damage around the afflicted enemy. This field of static is not only an offensive measure but also a defensive one, subtly disrupting incoming projectiles and reducing their impact. In addition, Skulker gains passive damage reduction against ranged attacks, reflecting his resilience in the face of technological assault. The energy manifests visually as flickering green sparks emanating from Skulker's armor, intensifying with each stack of 'Static Cling' applied to an enemy.
abilities.flavorQuote: "Feel that tingle? It's your system crashing."

Level 200: While fused, Skulker gains immunity to crowd control effects, becoming an unstoppable force on the battlefield. If the form is lost prematurely, Skulker gains a 500 + (0.3*X) shield for 5 seconds, mitigating the immediate vulnerability of reverting to base form, where X represents Skulker's current level.
abilities.description: Skulker overrides his ecto-skeleton with Technus' advanced technology, becoming the Ghostly Upgrade 9.9 for 15 seconds. While upgraded, Skulker's raw power surges, granting him 30% bonus HP and a 20% increase to both attack and magic attack, amplifying his combat potential. Every basic attack during this fusion applies a stack of 'Overload' to the target. Once a target accumulates 3 stacks of Overload, they are momentarily stunned for 1 second by the overwhelming energy. Each of Skulker's auto attacks also deals an additional 50 plus (0.1 * X) bonus magic damage, further electrifying the battlefield with each strike, where X represents Skulker's current level. Furthermore, while fused, Skulker's tactical options are enhanced: Spectral Trap Launcher now deploys not one, but three spectral traps in a tight cone, increasing zone denial capabilities. Ecto-Net Barrage's range and cone angle are doubled, effectively ensnaring a wider area in spectral nets. However, this powerful fusion is not without its risks. If Skulker's health plummets below 25% while fused, the form destabilizes, and the upgrade is lost, forcing Skulker to revert to his base form. Ghostly Upgrade 9.9 has a cooldown of 90 seconds.

abilities.description: Skulker's cybernetic enhancements and relentless focus grant him resilience and elusive maneuvering. He starts with 25 tenacity, mitigating the duration of incoming crowd control effects, and enjoys a 10% evasion chance, allowing him to nimbly dodge incoming attacks. Each time Skulker successfully inflicts a crowd control effect (such as a stun, snare, or silence) on an enemy, he gains one stack of 'Adaptive Protocols', up to a maximum of five stacks. Each stack of Adaptive Protocols bolsters Skulker's defensive capabilities, granting a 3% damage reduction against all incoming damage sources, capping at a 15% total reduction. This potent combination of tenacity, evasion, and damage reduction significantly increases Skulker's survivability. However, to maintain optimal efficiency, the Adaptive Protocols gradually recalibrate: stacks decay one at a time every 5 seconds, forcing Skulker to consistently apply crowd control to maintain his defensive edge.

character_v1.playstyle: Skulker is a tank who uses his zone control abilities and traps to lock down areas and disrupt enemies, protecting his team. His adaptability through Hunter's Arsenal allows him to tailor his defense.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Skulker synergizes well with damage dealers who can capitalize on his crowd control, and benefits from supports who can keep him alive while he sets up his zones.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Skulker's kit revolves around setting up zones with Spectral Trap Launcher and Ecto-Net Barrage. Hunter's Adaptation allows him to tailor his kit to be more tanky or disruptive. SkulTech 9.9 provides a powerful offensive burst.

character_v1.playstyle: Stan Marsh is a controller, debilitating enemies with debuffs and reducing their offensive capabilities. His kit revolves around the '****ed Up!' mechanic, lowering enemy damage output and disrupting their strategies, making him a solid enabler.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Stan pairs well with damage dealers who can capitalize on debuffed enemies. His shields and speed buff further enhance team survivability and damage output, making him a versatile support.
character_v1.tierSummary: Stan's controller kit is severely disjointed, lacking cohesive synergy between his debuff application ('Aw, Awww!') and the underwhelming payoff of 'Dude, This is Pretty Serious!'. His reliance on the 'Pissed Off!' status, which is easily cleansed or resisted, renders his control unreliable compared to peers like (hypothetical superior controller). The 'Serious, Dude' stun provides brief respite but suffers from single-target focus in an AoE-centric meta. The passive tenacity buff from 'Dude, Weak' offers minimal team utility, failing to elevate him above bottom-tier characters who provide more immediate and impactful support. 'OH MY GOD, THEY KILLED KENNY!!' ultimate is a desperate attempt at impact, but its delayed execution and reliance on setup makes it too easily countered for reliable comeback potential.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Stan's abilities are designed to apply and capitalize on the '****ed Up!' debuff. 'Aw, Awww! The Dude's Exasperation' and 'Dude, This is Pretty ****ed Up Right Here' apply initial stacks, while his passive shields allies upon full stacks. His Ultimate delivers a potent burst application, synergizing with his evasive signature passive.

character_v1.playstyle: Disruptive Debuffer & Support
character_v1.teamSynergy: Wendy excels in teams that can capitalize on her debuffs and buffs. character_v1.tierSummary: Wendy's bruiser role is undermined by a kit lacking focus; inconsistent damage, weak crowd control, and a situational ultimate fail to establish a clear identity. Her defensive passive, Dignified Resolve, is insufficient to compensate for her low base HP and unremarkable defensive stats relative to other bruisers. Compared to her tier peers like Rocko and Aeris, Wendy offers less impactful disruption or sustained damage output. Her signature passive, Debate Club Veteran, offers unreliable crowd control mitigation. In essence, Wendy requires a complete rework to establish a competitive niche.

abilities.description: Kyubey manifests a fleeting, ethereal contract before a targeted foe, offering a Faustian pact couched in subtle manipulations. Upon activation, Kyubey gestures, forming a glowing, spectral contract directly in front of the selected enemy combatant. This 'contract' doesn't inflict direct damage in the conventional sense; instead, it applies a stacking debuff called 'Entropic Burden.' Each stack of Entropic Burden reduces the target's outgoing healing and damage resistances against subsequent magical attacks, representing the subtle erosion of their willpower and the growing influence of Kyubey's offer. The potency of the healing reduction and the debuff's duration scales dynamically with Kyubey's Wisdom stat, embodying his ability to subtly and persistently influence those around him. Furthermore, at specific thresholds of accumulated Entropic Burden stacks, the enemy becomes slightly more susceptible to critical hits from Kyubey's allies. This insidious ability reflects Kyubey's nature, trading immediate power for long-term strategic advantage, slowly but surely tilting the odds in his team's favor through cunning manipulation rather than brute force. Successfully applying Entropic Burden also grants Kyubey a small, temporary shield as he feeds on the target's despair.

abilities.description: With a disarming smile, Kyubey presents an 'Enticing Offer', a pact promising great power at a hidden cost, bestowing a 'Contract' upon a single chosen ally for a duration of 8 seconds. This Contract amplifies the ally's combat prowess, increasing their damage output by a substantial 30% and bolstering their resilience, granting them 20% increased healing received from all sources. However, the path to power is paved with hardship; every 2 seconds while under Contract, the ally accumulates 1 stack of 'Despair'. Each stack of Despair inflicts a gradual erosion, diminishing healing output by 5% per stack and attack by 3% per stack. This insidious effect can accumulate up to a maximum of 10 stacks, representing a significant downturn in combat effectiveness if left unchecked. Should Kyubey choose to renew a Contract upon an ally already bound by its terms, he can extend the contract for an additional 4 seconds, refreshing the timer and maintaining the enhanced benefits, but at a steep price, instantly inflicting 2 stacks of 'Despair' upon the target as a forewarning of the ultimate price to pay. Kyubey, ever pragmatic, can cast this Contract upon himself, albeit at a reduced effectiveness of 50%, offering a glimpse into the power he bestows upon others.

abilities.description: Kyubey extends a paw, offering a subtly twisted boon. If the target is already a contracted Magical Girl, Kyubey focuses his attention on their Soul Gem, mending it with condensed potential. This process immediately heals the target for an amount equal to X, scaling with Kyubey's magic attack, followed by continuous healing for the same amount over the next 3 seconds, effectively doubling the initial heal. Simultaneously, Kyubey subtly reduces the weight of their despair, removing 2 stacks of 'Despair'. However, if the target is not currently bound by a contract, Kyubey, ever eager for new possibilities, applies 1 stack of 'Despair', dangling the promise of power before them. The restorative effects on contracted targets are tempered by their accumulated despair; each stack of 'Despair' reduces the healing by 20%, adding to Kyubey's strategic advantage. If, by some rare chance, the target has managed to avoid despair entirely, Kyubey, recognizing their untapped potential, grants them a shield, absorbing damage equal to 10% of their maximum HP for 5 seconds, a tempting glimpse of the power they could wield, driving them toward a contract.

abilities.description: Kyubey, ever the shrewd facilitator of magical girl contracts, passively accumulates 5 'potential' every second, a resource vital for manipulating fate and empowering his allies. Any ally currently under the effect of Kyubey's 'Contract' also contributes to this accumulation, passively generating an additional 2 'potential' per second for Kyubey. This 'potential' fuels Kyubey's abilities: 'Enticing Offer' requires 30 potential, 'Soul Gem Resonance' demands 20, and 'Inhibition Field' drains 50. Should Kyubey's potential fall below the cost of an ability, he will be unable to activate it, his machinations temporarily stalled. Furthermore, when an ally's Despair stacks reach the breaking point of 10, Kyubey harvests this negative energy, instantly gaining 50 potential, furthering his long-term goals. Finally, whenever an ally under the 'Contract' status succumbs to despair and dies, Kyubey absorbs a portion of their magical energy, permanently increasing his magic attack by 10 and resetting all his active ability cooldowns, allowing him to immediately capitalize on the chaos of battle.

abilities.description: Kyubey, the emotionless Incubator, operates with detached resolve, subtly manipulating events to maintain the universe's energy balance. His inherent detachment grants him a base resilience of 15 tenacity and 10 evasion, subtly deflecting incoming attacks. Allies currently under the effects of 'Contract,' forged through granting magical girl wishes, find their burdens eased, redirecting 10% of the damage Kyubey receives to themselves, bypassing both shields and damage reduction. This redirection represents Kyubey's casual disregard for individual suffering in pursuit of his goals. However, if Kyubey himself is under the effect of 'Contract,' perhaps through unforeseen consequences or interference, the redirected damage is halved to 5%, reflecting the compromised efficiency of his schemes. Each stack of 'Despair' weighing upon Kyubey, representing the disillusionment and suffering he causes, weakens his magical capabilities by decreasing his 'magic atk' by 2% per stack. Yet, paradoxically, this despair reinforces his resolve, granting him 3 tenacity per stack. At the threshold of 10 stacks of 'Despair,' Kyubey achieves a chilling stoicism, becoming immune to stuns as the weight of his actions solidifies his determination. However, this state is unsustainable; he accumulates 1 stack of 'Despair' every 5 seconds, a constant reminder of the endless cycle of hope and despair he perpetuates. Further highlighting his detached nature, Kyubey is utterly incapable of healing himself directly, relying solely on external sources to maintain his existence and continue his machinations.

character_v1.playstyle: Kyubey is a manipulative healer, focusing on long-term strategic buffs at the cost of applying the Despair status. Effective play requires careful management of Despair stacks and synergistic team compositions to mitigate negative effects, favoring calculated risks for high rewards.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Kyubey synergizes well with teams that can capitalize on the damage boost from 'Contract' and mitigate the negative effects of 'Despair,' such as through cleanses, shields, or damage mitigation. He is especially effective with allies who can heal themselves or benefit from increased healing received, but his passive damage redirection demands a team that can also protect him.
character_v1.tierSummary: Kyubey's kit, while thematically appropriate, suffers from severe mechanical disjointedness, rendering his support capabilities unreliable within the current meta. The character's primary 'heal', Incentivized Offering, is conditional and often detrimental, undermining its intended purpose and demonstrating poor synergy with his passive energy generation. Compared to dedicated healers, Kyubey lacks consistent, impactful healing output, exacerbated by his reliance on enemy despair states. Inhibition Field's inconsistent debuff application further diminishes Kyubey's control potential, placing him significantly below peers with more streamlined and effective support kits, particularly in the crowded B tier.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Kyubey's kit revolves around applying 'Contract' to allies, boosting their damage and healing received at the cost of accumulating 'Despair'. He can mitigate 'Despair' with 'Soul Gem Resonance,' but must carefully manage his energy. The 'Inhibition Field' further amplifies the risk-reward dynamic, and the 'Emotionless Observer' passive gives Kyubey both offensive and defensive scaling with Despair.

These bonuses stack additively, creating a potent combination of enhanced spell power and increased critical damage. However, when Angela casts no Arcane Threads to ally nor enemy, her focus becomes acute and precise, granting her a flat 10% increase to her critical hit chance. This allows her to deliver more consistent bursts of damage, even when not directly engaging in threading maneuvers. By strategically managing her Arcane Threads on friend and foe, Angela becomes a versatile force on the battlefield, adapting her damage profile to suit the situation. (Patch) Enhanced flexibility: This ability now features increased jack-of-all-trades interactions, providing expanded utility in a variety of combat scenarios.
abilities.description: Angela's ever-present chimes resonate with protective magic, offering subtle but pervasive aid to her allies, bolstering them against the relentless onslaught of their foes. Each allied hero benefits from a continuous blessing, granting them 10 tenacity, steadfastly reducing the duration of disabling crowd control effects that threaten to impede their movements and strategies. Further, the chimes weave a delicate barrier around each ally, providing a shield capable of absorbing 30 points of incoming damage. This resilient shield diligently regenerates at a rate of 5 points every second while the ally remains out of combat, ensuring sustained protection during periods of respite. When Angela actively intervenes, channeling her Arcane Thread toward a teammate, she amplifies their defensive posture, enveloping them in an Echoing Barrier that absorbs an additional 75 damage for a duration of 4 seconds. This potent surge of protection significantly increases their survivability against immediate threats. Conversely, when Angela focuses her Arcane Thread upon an enemy, she destabilizes their focus and weakens their attacks, reducing their damage output by 5% for a duration of 4 seconds. This strategic application of her powers subtly shifts the balance of power, diminishing the enemy's offensive capabilities. Angela's passive presence ensures that her support extends far beyond direct intervention, providing consistent, team-wide advantages that enhance both their offensive and defensive capabilities.

character_v1.playstyle: Angela's kit is designed to enable allies and disable enemies, staying true to her Mystic Guardian role. Her abilities focus on manipulating the battlefield with Arcane Threads, offering buffs, heals, and debuffs that require careful planning and execution. Her complexity comes from managing these threads and understanding the conditional nature of her abilities.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Angela excels in teams that benefit from sustained buffs, debuffs, and healing. Her ultimate provides crucial protection and damage amplification, making her an ideal support for damage-focused compositions.
character_v1.tierSummary: Angela's S-tier status is propped up almost entirely by 'Cosmic Weave: Celestial Barrier,' a kit-defining ultimate offering unparalleled cleanse, shield, and CC immunity. However, her reliance on this single ability for viability reveals a glaring lack of synergy between the rest of her kit and the support role, especially when compared to tier peers. 'Crystallized Restraint,' while potent, suffers from delayed execution, making it unreliable against faster compositions common in the current meta. Arcane Echoes, while a strong passive, it's also unreliable when needing to protect allies on low health, due to the percentage based evasion and tenacity buffs. Overall, Angela is easily countered by compositions that bait out or disrupt 'Celestial Barrier,' rendering her largely ineffective; her tier placement is suspect and likely inflated by initial burst power.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Angela's kit revolves around the 'Arcane Thread' mechanic. Her abilities synergize by extending the duration and enhancing the effects of these threads, creating a playstyle that rewards strategic planning and resource management.

Furthermore, Vivian's innate resilience grants her 20 tenacity, reducing the duration of crowd control effects applied to her. character_v1.playstyle: Vivian is a damage dealer that focuses on empowering allies and debuffing enemies through temporary enchantment infusions. Her kit requires strategic management of stone resources and a good understanding of equipment stat scaling to maximize effectiveness.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Vivian synergizes well with damage dealers who can capitalize on the 'Fortuitous Strike' debuff, and with allies who benefit greatly from the stat buffs provided by 'Weapon Scaling: Agility Shift' and the 'Stone Infusion' ultimate. Her support is best utilized in compositions that can consistently apply basic attacks to trigger her passive stacks.
character_v1.tierSummary: Vivian's damage output is middling for an A-tier, hampered by reliance on unreliable buffs (Agility Shift) and conditional procs (Stone Resonance). While Resonance: Attuned Barrier offers moderate support, it doesn't compensate for her inconsistent damage application compared to peers like dedicated damage dealers in S- or A+. Unstable Aegis: Magic Misfire's stun is unreliable, further limiting her disruptive potential. She's outperformed by more consistent damage-focused units, and her hybrid role is executed better by more specialized support characters; a cohesive identity is lacking, causing her kit's synergy to fall flat and contributing to her placement in the overcrowded A-tier.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Vivian's kit revolves around empowering allies and debuffing enemies using the 'Fortuitous Strike' mechanic. 'Mystic's Intuition' feeds into 'Stone Infusion', creating a rewarding gameplay loop where maximizing 'Fortuitous Strike' uptime leads to stronger ultimates.

He then unleashes this raw force in a sweeping melee attack aimed at a single target within melee range. The attack's damage is amplified by a random elemental modifier; fire, water, earth, air or electric adding a percentage of elemental damage to the skill. The physical impact also generates a small area-of-effect blast, knocking back nearby enemies a modest distance and potentially disrupting their actions. The instability of the energy grants a minor shield, while allies within the area of effect receive a small boost to their movement speed. character_v1.playstyle: Ben Tennyson in Alien Force is a versatile character who excels at adapting to any situation. His kit revolves around strategic form-swapping, making him a jack-of-all-trades capable of filling multiple roles. His effectiveness hinges on cooldown management and understanding which alien form best suits the current scenario.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Ben benefits from allies who can capitalize on his flexible abilities, such as damage amplifiers or those who can enable his transformations through crowd control. He can disrupt enemy formations with Humungousaur's knockback, deal sustained damage with Swampfire's burn, or evade threats to buy time for his team.
character_v1.tierSummary: Ben Tennyson, stuck in C-tier, suffers from diluted jack-of-all-trades syndrome; his kit lacks the focus necessary for impactful performance in any specific role. While "Hero Time" offers burst potential, its reliance on short Omnitrix cooldowns is insufficient to elevate his overall damage output or control capabilities compared to specialized peers. Swampfire's regeneration is negligible, and the reactive shift is inconsistently impactful due to his low base stats. Ultimately, Ben's kit provides no compelling reason to select him over higher-performing characters with clear strengths.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Ben's kit encourages strategic form-swapping, utilizing the Omnitrix Cooldown to maximize the Adaptive Omnitrix Matrix buff. 'Hero Time' allows for rapid transformations and shield generation, complementing his defensive repositioning from Alien Reflexes.

character_v1.playstyle: Bruce Wayne excels as a buffer, controlling the battlefield with debuffs, stealth, and strategic counterattacks. His 'Preparedness' mechanic rewards players who anticipate and react to enemy movements, providing critical openings for allies.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Bruce Wayne excels at disrupting enemy formations and providing openings for his allies. His debuffs from 'Batarang Barrage' and the 'Targeted' debuff from 'World's Greatest Detective' make enemies more vulnerable, while 'The Knight Falls' provides area-of-effect damage and speed buffs for allies.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Bruce Wayne's abilities synergize by generating and consuming 'Preparedness'. 'Evasive Maneuvers' and 'Underestimated Intellect' generate it, while 'Batarang Barrage' and 'The Knight Falls' consume it for enhanced effects. This encourages a playstyle of strategic resource management and calculated counterattacks.

As the invincibility fades and she reverts to her normal form, Bobette projects a wave of festive cheer, granting herself a protective shield that absorbs damage equal to 10% of her maximum health, lasting for 5 seconds. character_v1.playstyle: Dandy is a support character that can transition into a bruiser. His abilities focus on buffing allies and manipulating the economy, with the option to transform into a more aggressive Twisted form using Ichor Reserves.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Dandy excels in teams that can consistently secure kills, maximizing the benefits of his signature passive. His shield and heal provide sustain, while his transformation offers burst damage and crowd control. He works well with damage-focused compositions that can capitalize on his buffs and support.
character_v1.tierSummary: Dandy's S-tier placement is questionable; while his support kit offers a unique blend of utility and resource management with 'Dandy's Bargain' and 'Ichor Dividend,' his direct impact on the fight pales in comparison to peers like Minnie Mouse who offer more consistent and potent buffs. 'Prismatic Bloom' has burst potential, but the high Ichor cost and transformation delay make it unreliable in the current meta dominated by faster, more decisive ultimates. He's essentially a discount enabler in a landscape where raw power and immediate effect reign supreme; requiring too much setup for debatable returns. His reliance on specific ability timings for maximum value, particularly with 'Ichor Dividend' scaling, leaves him vulnerable to disruption and outpaced by simpler, more effective support options.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Dandy's kit revolves around generating and spending Ichor Reserves. His passive and first two abilities help him generate Ichor, while his ultimate consumes it for a powerful transformation. His signature passive further rewards team success, creating a positive feedback loop.

abilities.description: Channeling his desperate knowledge of guerilla warfare, Kyle Reese quickly crafts a devastating pipe bomb, a crude but effective weapon born from the ashes of a ruined future. He expertly hurls this makeshift explosive towards a targeted location, the device arcing through the air like a harbinger of destruction. Upon impact with the ground or reaching the apex of its trajectory, the pipe bomb emits a series of rapid, urgent beeps, signaling its imminent detonation. After a nerve-wracking 1.5-second delay, the pipe bomb erupts in a cataclysmic explosion. The blast inflicts X + (1.1 * atk) physical damage to all enemies caught within a 25-unit radius; 'X' representing the base damage and 'atk' scaling with Reese's attack stat, ensuring relevance throughout a fight. The explosive concussive force not only wounds but also incapacitates, stunning all afflicted foes for 1.75 seconds. While stunned, they are helpless, unable to move, attack, or use any abilities, leaving them exposed to further attacks. Given its 55-second cooldown, strategic placement and timing are crucial to maximize the potential devastation of the Pipe Bomb Takedown, and to ensure the survival of Reese and his squad.

character_v1.playstyle: Kyle Reese is a protective support character who enhances an ally's survivability while disrupting the enemy team. His abilities allow him to quickly move in and out of danger, providing cover fire and tactical advantages to his team.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Kyle synergizes well with damage dealers who benefit from increased survivability and disruption. He can protect fragile carries while providing them with an atk boost through Guardian Protocol upgrades. His Flashbangs and Pipe Bomb Detonation can set up opportunities for other team members to capitalize on.
character_v1.tierSummary: Kyle Reese's A tier placement is propped up by Guardian Protocol and Tech-Com Evasion Training which patch up team-wide survivability issues. However, his kit lacks cohesive synergy; Pipe Bomb's zone control conflicts with his buffering role, and Flashbang is easily countered, hamstringing his utility. Compared to peers like Sakura Haruno who offer more consistent healing or Frog's superior tanking, Kyle's contribution is often diluted. While his numbers aren't bad, his niche is too muddled, and he needs better ability scaling or a kit rework to climb higher.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Kyle's kit revolves around protecting his designated Ward. Suppressive Fire and Flashbang Grenades allow him to control the battlefield, while his ultimate provides a strong burst of damage and crowd control to turn the tide of battle. Tech-Com Evasion Training ensures he can quickly react to threats and reposition to defend his Ward.

character_v1.playstyle: Itachi excels at quickly eliminating high-priority targets through strategic use of Genjutsu and Mangekyō Sharingan abilities, requiring precise timing and tactical awareness to maximize damage output and control the battlefield. character_v1.teamSynergy: Itachi works well with teams that can provide additional crowd control or damage amplification, allowing him to maximize his burst damage potential. He excels at picking off high-priority targets, making him a valuable asset in team fights and skirmishes. Teammates that can capitalize on the Magic Defense reduction from Tsukuyomi will further enhance his effectiveness.
character_v1.tierSummary: Itachi's A-tier placement is questionable given the current meta; his delayed burst from Amaterasu and Susanoo, while potent, are easily countered, leaving him vulnerable compared to more immediate assassins. The 'Crow Clone/Tsukuyomi' combo is telegraphed and lacks the setup speed required to consistently punish meta threats. Eternal Mangekyō provides marginal scaling that doesn't compensate for his susceptibility to burst damage and control. He occupies an assassin slot oversaturated with faster, safer, and more impactful options; his reliance on specific ability sequencing makes him predictable and ultimately less viable than other A-tier peers such as Puss in Boots, Trunks, Richard, and Kyubey.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Itachi's kit revolves around the synergy between Tsukuyomi and Amaterasu, allowing for high burst damage when combined. Mangekyō Resonance further amplifies his abilities, rewarding skillful ability usage and strategic decision-making. The Crow Clone Technique provides mobility and utility, while Susanoo serves as a powerful offensive and defensive tool.

abilities.description: Jesse, fueled by nervous energy and a touch of desperation, whips up a batch of his signature product, launching a vial of potent, modified crystal meth at a single, targeted enemy. Upon impact, the vial shatters, dealing an initial 60 magic attack damage directly to the target, momentarily stunning them with the sheer chemical force. Following this initial hit, the targeted enemy is afflicted with 'Bad Cook,' a debilitating status effect that lasts for 4 seconds. 'Bad Cook' causes the target to suffer 20 magic attack damage per second, simulating the internal chaos of a botched recipe. But the effects don't stop there; while under the influence of 'Bad Cook,' the target experiences a 20% reduction in all incoming healing, as their body struggles to cope with Jesse's twisted formula. The real potency of 'Yo, Science!' lies in Jesse's own 'Chemistry' skill. If Jesse's 'Chemistry' talent is at 3 or more stacks, indicating a period of focused and productive cooking, the 'Bad Cook' effect intensifies; the targeted enemy suffers an additional 10% damage from all sources for the duration of the burn, representing their vulnerability to Jesse's perfected recipe. Conversely, if Jesse's 'Chemistry' skill falls below 0 stacks, revealing his distraction or ineptitude, the initial burst of damage is reduced by 50%, showcasing the flawed nature of his creation. Rather than suffering from the burning damage, the target instead experiences a twisted form of aid, receiving healing equal to 1% of their maximum health per second while afflicted by 'Bad Cook,' a paradoxical consequence of Jesse's chaotic cooking.

abilities.description: Jesse, with his street smarts and intuitive grasp of volatile situations, instinctively analyzes the ebb and flow of combat, reacting with uncanny precision. Every 15 seconds, Jesse's HUD displays a 'reading' of the current battlefield state, represented by one of three potential outcomes: 'Hot,' 'Cold,' or 'Neutral,' reflecting the temperature of the conflict. By accurately predicting the immediate consequences of each reading, Jesse gains a 'Clarity' stack, symbolizing his heightened awareness and control. A correct assessment grants 1 'Clarity' stack, indicating his growing focus, while an incorrect assessment causes him to lose 1 'Clarity' stack, reflecting his wavering attention. These stacks are persistent yet volatile, embodying Jesse's fluctuating state of mind, and range from -5 to 5. As Jesse levels up, the predictive challenge intensifies, requiring him to adapt and refine his tactics. For each 'Clarity' stack, Jesse gains 1% tenacity and 0.5% evasion, up to a maximum of 5% tenacity and 2.5% evasion when he reaches 5 stacks, underscoring his resilience and agility. Conversely, negative stacks reflect Jesse's growing disorientation, reducing his tenacity and making him more vulnerable to crowd control effects.

character_v1.playstyle: Jesse is designed as a volatile support character whose effectiveness depends on correctly predicting chemical reactions, enabling both support and disruptive builds. His focus leans toward a support role, providing buffs and debuffs that can be enhanced through successful Chemistry stacks.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Jesse synergizes well with teams that can capitalize on the buffs and debuffs he provides, such as attack-damage heavy compositions or burst damage comps. His ultimate enables him to lock in a desired chemical state and augment his support/damage output.
character_v1.tierSummary: Jesse Pinkman's kit suffers from severe anti-synergy, oscillating between weak, redundant fire damage and anemic supportive abilities that fail to meaningfully impact engagements. Compared to other supports, his utility is negligible; 'Yo, Science!' is easily avoided and provides minimal area denial, while 'Blue Sky Blitz' offers unreliable damage and healing. His passive is statistically insignificant, and his ultimate, 'Yeah, Bitch! Chemical Firestorm,' is too slow and telegraphed to reliably land, further cementing his position as a bottom-tier character. The lack of cohesive strategy renders him completely outclassed by peers who provide consistent, reliable support or damage output.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Jesse's kit revolves around the Chemistry mechanic, where positive stacks boost offensive capabilities and shield, and negative stacks boost sustain. The success of his abilities is determined by the players capacity to manipulate Chemistry, rewarding strategic choices.

character_v1.playstyle: Darth Vader excels as a control-oriented tank, using his Force abilities to disrupt enemies, absorb damage, and control the battlefield. character_v1.teamSynergy: Darth Vader synergizes well with teams that can capitalize on his disruptive abilities and provide additional survivability. Allies that can provide healing or shields can further enhance Vader's ability to generate Hatred and withstand incoming damage. Damage dealers who benefit from controlled enemies, such as those stunned or pulled by 'Force Choke' and 'I Find Your Lack of Faith Disturbing', can maximize their effectiveness. Additionally, allies that can inflict Crowd Control effects can help Vader generate more Hatred, further amplifying his abilities.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Darth Vader's kit revolves around managing Hatred stacks, which are generated through damage taken, damage dealt, and specific abilities. This creates a cohesive playstyle where Vader must balance aggression with defense, using 'Deflecting Strikes' to absorb damage and generate Hatred, then expending it with 'Force Choke' or 'I Find Your Lack of Faith Disturbing' for amplified effects. 'Boundless Rage' provides a constant source of Hatred, making him more resilient and powerful as he endures enemy attacks. 'Sith Meditation' enhances Vader's Crowd Control resilience, while also bolstering his Hatred generation when subjected to debuffs.

character_v1.playstyle: Luke Skywalker is designed as a damage dealer with significant utility and support capabilities, fitting his role as a Jedi. His abilities balance aggressive lightsaber combat with strategic Force abilities to empower both himself and his team.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Luke provides damage and moderate utility to his team. His 'Force Push Barrage' can disrupt enemy formations, and 'Jedi Resilience' enhances his survivability, allowing him to stay in the fight longer and support allies. Luke is also a strong choice as a carry hero.
character_v1.tierSummary: Luke's kit suffers from a disjointed identity, mixing damage and control elements without excelling at either, leaving him outclassed within the damage roster. His damage output is moderate, but lacks the burst or consistency required to compete with higher-tier damage dealers, and his control is unreliable due to limited status duration and susceptibility to tenacity. The Force Potential resource mechanic offers minimal impact, failing to meaningfully enhance Luke's core capabilities in the face of more impactful passives. Jedi Resilience provides negligible survivability, offering only a small shield that is easily broken in the current meta's damage-heavy environment, rendering Luke a suboptimal choice compared to specialized damage characters or more robust controllers.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Luke's abilities are designed to synergize around building and expending Force Attunement. 'Flashing Blade Assault' generates Attunement, while 'Force Push Barrage' expends it for control. His Ultimate consumes all Attunement for a massive burst. The passive provides sustain and baseline generation.

character_v1.playstyle: Han Solo excels as a skirmisher, using his mobility and blaster skills to disrupt enemy formations while supporting allies with well-timed debuffs. His kit encourages aggressive positioning and skillful resource management of Smuggler's Luck stacks to maximize damage and utility.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Han Solo synergizes well with teammates who can apply status effects, increasing the effectiveness of 'Quick Draw Blaster Shot'. He also benefits from allies who can capitalize on the 'Marked' and 'Disrupt' debuffs. He provides a solid mix of sustained damage and utility, making him a versatile addition to most team compositions.
character_v1.tierSummary: Han Solo's C-tier status is cemented by his kit's lack of cohesive synergy; 'Lucky Shot' is his only reliable damage source, while the rest is diluted utility. Compared to skirmisher peers and the broader roster, his damage output and survivability are subpar, rendering him a liability. The inconsistent 'Never Tell Me The Odds' and unreliable 'Evade and Outmaneuver' fail to compensate for his glaring weaknesses. His theoretical 'DL-44 Barrage' AoE is neutered by targeting limitations, making him a fundamentally flawed character.

'Never Tell Me The Odds' provides sustain and Smuggler's Luck, fueling his other abilities. Smuggler's Tenacity improves survivability. The 'DL-44 Barrage' Ultimate can be empowered by consuming stacks of Smuggler's Luck.

character_v1.playstyle: Leia is designed as a versatile jack-of-all-trades, shifting between support and damage roles using 'Diplomatic Influence'. Her abilities allow her to buff allies and debuff enemies, positioning her as a tactical battlefield commander.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Leia provides significant team-wide buffs, enhancing attack damage, attack speed, and damage reduction. Her shield and debuff abilities offer targeted support and control, making her a valuable asset in various team compositions. Allies who benefit from attack speed and damage amplification will particularly synergize well with Leia's kit.
character_v1.tierSummary: Leia's kit, while synergistic on paper with its reliance on team-wide buffs and targeted support, suffers from inflated stat dependencies and underperforming scaling relative to current S-tier peers like Android 18. Her 'Hope for the Rebellion' aura provides a marginal attack boost, yet is outclassed by dedicated support characters offering superior, more impactful buffs. 'Rebel Command: Blaster Barrage' demonstrates poor damage output despite its debuffing potential, failing to provide the necessary burst needed for control. Though she's meant to be a jack-of-all-trades, the abilities are subpar, and thus, the 'Galaxy to Fight For' passive lacks proper utility. Leia's viability hinges heavily on substantial stat rebalancing or significant skill modifier improvements.

tips: Prioritize building HP: 'Rebel Tactics: Cover Fire' scales with Leia's max HP, making her primary tanking stat also feed her support role.
Time Diplomatic Influence expenditure: Use 'Rebel Tactics' and 'Rebellion's Resolve' strategically to maximize their benefits (shielding, crit chance, CC immunity).

Manage Rebel Coordination effectively: Debuff high-priority targets with 'Rebel Command: Blaster Barrage' to reduce their armor and magic resistance, especially when you have 50 Rebel Coordination available.
strategyData.overview: Princess Leia is a jack-of-all-trades character that focuses on buffing her allies and debuffing enemies. She relies on Diplomatic Influence and Rebel Coordination to amplify her abilities. Managing these resources effectively is crucial. She can be a strong pick but requires careful planning and execution to maximize her potential, because she cannot take a punch.
strategyData.counterplay: Focus fire on Leia to prevent her from buffing allies and debuffing enemies. CC her to interrupt her ability usage and prevent resource generation. Burst her down with high damage dealers, as she has low base HP and relies on shields for survivability. Abilities that remove shields are also effective.

character_v1.playstyle: Lop excels at controlling the battlefield by alternating between supporting allies with buffs and disrupting enemies with debuffs. Resource management and strategic stance switching are key to maximizing her effectiveness.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Lop thrives in a team composition that benefits from increased survivability and disruption. She pairs exceptionally well with damage-focused allies who can capitalize on the advantages granted by Elders' Vigilance.
character_v1.tierSummary: Lop's kit, theoretically a controller, lacks the hard CC or sustained utility necessary to effectively manipulate the battlefield, relegating her to a glorified, understatted support. Compared to other C-tier controllers, her control options are weaker and less reliable, with Adaptable Anomaly's stance change being too slow to meaningfully impact fights. The synergy between her abilities is minimal; Caravan's Cover provides a weak shield while Elders' Vigilance, her ultimate, offers negligible debuff utility. Ultimately, Lop fails to carve a niche, being outclassed in both support and control by roster peers, rendering her unviable in competitive play.

tips: Abuse the short range of Steadfast Bloom to bait enemies closer to your allies, as she wants to brawl and will be more effective when near others.
Keep Force Potential in mind when using Leap of Tao and Lightsaber Reflection; play around the buffs based on your team comp.

Prioritize supportive actions (shielding, healing, buffing) early on to build Force Potential quickly, and then switch to disruptive actions (slowing, stunning, taunting) to maintain a balanced state.
strategyData.overview: Lop is a controller who wants to play aggressively while also being close to her teammates. Her Force Potential passive makes her kit highly variable, but also predictable. Adapt to each game state and exploit enemy positioning, but ultimately you'll struggle to carry.
strategyData.counterplay: Punish her for diving in without her team. CC her to prevent her from taunting or shielding allies. Kite her to prevent her from getting Force Potential.

character_v1.playstyle: Azula is designed as a controller, leveraging her ability to accumulate Combustion stacks to unleash potent area-of-effect stuns and damage. While the original concept suggested an assassin, her area control and the need to build stacks over time better suits the controller role.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Azula excels in teams that can capitalize on her crowd control. Allies who can quickly follow up on her stuns or benefit from reduced enemy damage output synergize well with her. Characters that can provide additional shields or healing can also help her maintain stacks and survive engagements.
character_v1.tierSummary: Azula's kit, while visually appealing, suffers from fractured synergy, failing to establish her as a top-tier crowd controller. Her 'Dazzling Fire Jet Propulsion' offers mobility but lacks reliable follow-up, and 'Lightning Flick Disruption' struggles to consistently apply its disruptive status. Compared to A-tier controllers like Kevin Levin, Azula's control is less consistent and easily countered, hindering her ability to effectively manage the battlefield. The reliance on 'Controlled Fury' for scaling creates a feast-or-famine scenario, easily shut down by early-game aggression or tenacity stacking. 'Sozin's Comet Enhanced Inferno' provides burst, but its long channel time leaves her vulnerable, making it a situational, rather than defining, ability.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Azula's kit revolves around building Combustion stacks with Dazzling Fire Jet Propulsion and basic attacks, then expending them with Lightning Flick Disruption for burst damage and crowd control. Calculated Cruelty enhances her stats based on the number of stacks, incentivizing aggressive play. Sozin's Comet Enhanced Inferno provides a defensive buff and an area-of-effect burst, while Fear is the Only Reliable Way ensures consistent control.

abilities.description: Toph's mastery of earthbending and her profound connection to the ground grant her unparalleled resilience in battle. Each time Toph sustains damage from any source – be it physical attacks, elemental strikes, or even the smallest pebble underfoot – she attunes herself further to the vibrations around her, gaining a stack of 'Fortitude,' increasing her damage reduction by 3% for 4 seconds. This effect can stack up to 5 times, granting a maximum damage reduction of 15%, significantly reducing incoming damage. Each new stack of 'Fortitude' refreshes the duration of all existing stacks, ensuring a sustained defensive posture when under fire. Furthermore, Toph's inherent connection to the earth provides her with a flat bonus to Tenacity, reducing the duration of incoming debuffs by a fixed amount, as well as a flat bonus to Evasion, increasing her chance to completely avoid incoming attacks. This makes her a formidable presence on the battlefield, capable of weathering even the most relentless assaults. Toph's seismic sense extends her awareness beyond mere sight, transforming adversity into an opportunity to harden her resolve and fortify her defenses.

character_v1.playstyle: Toph excels at controlling the battlefield and providing vision, fitting the utility role perfectly. Her kit manipulates terrain and reveals enemies, offering both defensive and offensive options for her team.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Toph is an excellent utility pick, offering vision control and defensive capabilities. Her Earth Wall can protect vulnerable allies, while her slows and reveals help teammates focus fire on key targets. The damage amplification at high levels supports damage-heavy team comps.
character_v1.tierSummary: Toph's S-tier status stems from exceptional area control and defensive utility, enabled by Seismic Shelter and Earthly Fortitude augmenting survivability. Seismic Sense, despite nerfs, still provides crucial accuracy against stealth, setting her apart from peers like Android 18 in target acquisition. While Resolute Bind offers a burst option, its Wind element is thematically incongruent and strategically questionable. Toph's kit synergy shines in defensive stalemates, yet offensive shortcomings relegate her to a reactive, rather than proactive, role, limiting her true potential within the highly aggressive S-tier meta. Compared to Minnie Mouse, Toph sacrifices raw support power for increased battlefield presence.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Toph's kit revolves around using Seismic Sense for enhanced accuracy and vision, allowing her to disrupt and control enemies effectively. Earth Wall provides cover, while Tremorsense Strike slows down targets, making them easier to hit.

upgrades: Lv10: Increases Pride stack ATK bonus to 5% per stack and critical hit damage to 8%.

abilities.description: Saiyan Pride Assault embodies Vegeta's unyielding ambition and brutal fighting style. As a passive ability, whenever Vegeta lands a critical hit, he gains a stack of 'Pride,' up to a maximum of 5 stacks. Each stack of Pride increases his ATK by 3% and his Critical Hit Damage by 5%. Upon reaching 5 stacks, Vegeta enters a 'Saiyan Surge' state for 10 seconds. In this state, his attacks gain a 20% chance to inflict 'Bleed,' dealing a percentage of the target's maximum health as physical damage over 5 seconds. Furthermore, while in Saiyan Surge, Vegeta's next active ability cast has its cooldown reduced by 25%. This reflects Vegeta's aggressive desire to relentlessly overpower his foes. The potency of the bleed is directly influenced by Vegeta's ATK and critical hit stats, further incentivizing a damage-focused build. Finally, if Vegeta is critically hit while in Saiyan Surge, he unleashes a defiant Ki blast around him, dealing moderate AoE damage and consuming all Pride stacks. This ability represents Vegeta's raw power, aggressive playstyle, and his unending quest to surpass all others. The visual effect is of Vegeta glowing with a fierce, crackling aura upon entering Saiyan Surge.
abilities.flavorQuote: "I will not be outdone! Witness the power of a Saiyan Prince!"

character_v1.playstyle: Vegeta is a high-damage bruiser who thrives in prolonged combat, building up his Saiyan Pride to unleash increasingly devastating attacks. His kit rewards aggression and skillful resource management, allowing him to dominate the battlefield as his power grows.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Vegeta benefits from teammates who can provide consistent damage amplification or healing. He can also act as a secondary damage dealer, providing sustained pressure while other carries unleash their burst damage.
character_v1.tierSummary: Vegeta's kit suffers from disjointed scaling and inconsistent damage output, relegating him to low-tier status; his 'Saiyan Pride' mechanic is a trap, offering negligible benefits compared to other scaling passives. While 'Final Flash' provides burst AoE, its high-risk, high-cooldown nature is easily punished, rendering it unreliable in the current meta. 'Saiyan Rush' is statistically inferior to peers' multi-hit options, and his single-target damage lacks the necessary punch to threaten higher-tier characters. Fundamentally, Vegeta's design fails to capitalize on his intended damage role, making him a suboptimal choice in nearly every matchup.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Vegeta's kit revolves around the 'Saiyan Pride' mechanic, where dealing and taking damage fuels his abilities. His passive provides sustain and increased damage at low health, while his ultimate acts as a powerful finisher that consumes his accumulated Pride.

Furthermore, the initial exposure plants a seed of terror, inflicting one stack of 'Phobia', amplifying their existing dread and weakening their resolve. Each tick of this oppressive fog—occurring every second—subjects enemies still within the cloud to a fresh dose of the toxic nightmare, adding an additional 'Phobia' stack. However, even the deepest terrors have their limits; the maximum number of 'Phobia' stacks any single target can accumulate from this cloud is capped at three, preventing any one individual from succumbing completely to madness. This ensures the effects are crippling but not wholly insurmountable, allowing opponents avenues for counterplay and strategic repositioning amid the swirling shadows.

abilities.description: Scarecrow channels the primal fears lurking within every heart, unleashing a potent wave of terror that engulfs all enemies on the field. Each foe is immediately struck with 150 magic damage, amplified by 80% of Scarecrow's magic attack power, inducing a sharp, agonizing jolt of fear. This initial shock is merely the prelude; as the terror spreads, each enemy is afflicted with three stacks of 'Phobia,' weakening their resolve. Furthermore, the Scarecrow delves into the subconscious of each enemy, materializing their greatest anxieties into personalized 'Nightmare' debuffs, each lasting for a duration of 5 seconds. For enemies whose strength lies in brute force (highest Attack stat), the 'Horror' debuff manifests, crippling their critical strike chance by 30%. Those relying on resilience (highest Defense stat) are plagued by 'Paranoia,' diminishing their shield effectiveness by a quarter. Mages who command formidable magic (highest Magic Attack stat) succumb to 'Delusion,' their healing received slashed by 25%. Wizards whose arcane is built around durability (highest Magic Defense stat) are debuffed by 'Phobia', directly reducing their magic resistance by 15%. Swift warriors who rely on agility (highest Speed stat) are paralyzed by 'Panic,' their movement speed decreased by 30%. The Scarecrow's power twists each battle into a horrific mirror of the enemy's worst nightmare.
